You may also make it the faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that reveals an implied condition), because it is the answer to an implied condition, the implied form being "since their states are thus, leave Me". ذر is an imperative verb whose agent is latent (mustatir), implied as أنت, referring to the Messenger ﷺ; the yāʾ is in the position of an accusative as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The wāw is a conjunction and من is conjoined to the yāʾ; or the wāw is for accompaniment and من is in the position of an accusative as a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment); the first is preferable. The clause يكذب is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; بهذا is attached (mutaʿalliq) to يكذب, and الحديث is a badal (substitute) for the demonstrative. (سَنَسْتَدْرِجُهُمْ مِنْ حَيْثُ لا يَعْلَمُونَ) resumptive speech, introduced to explain the manner of the punishment conveyed in summary by the preceding command. The pronoun refers to من, and the plural is with regard to its meaning, just as the singular in يكذب is with regard to its wording. نستدرجهم is an imperfect verb, a latent agent and a mafʿūl bihi; من is a preposition and حيث an adverb indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma in the position of a genitive by من; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to نستدرجهم, and the clause لا يعلمون is in the position of a genitive by the adverb's being annexed to it. (وَأُمْلِي لَهُمْ إِنَّ كَيْدِي مَتِينٌ) the wāw is a conjunction, and أملي is an imperfect verb whose agent is latent, implied as أنا, because it is conjoined to سنستدرجهم; لهم is attached to أملي. الإملاء is granting respite and following up favours and blessings so that they will be deluded; the explanation of this figure of speech will come in the section on rhetoric. إنّ with its subject and its khabar (predicate); the clause serves as the reason for the granting of respite. (أَمْ تَسْئَلُهُمْ أَجْراً فَهُمْ مِنْ مَغْرَمٍ مُثْقَلُونَ) conjoined to what preceded in His words أم لهم شركاء, i.e. "or do you seek from them a recompense for the guidance and faith to which you call them?" تسألهم is an imperfect verb, a latent agent and a first object, and أجرا a second object. The fāʾ is a conjunction, هم a mubtadaʾ (subject), من مغرم attached to مثقلون, and مثقلون the khabar, i.e. burdened with a heavy load under which they stagger. (أَمْ عِنْدَهُمُ الْغَيْبُ فَهُمْ يَكْتُبُونَ) also conjoined. عندهم is an adverb attached to an omitted fronted khabar, and الغيب a postponed mubtadaʾ; the fāʾ is a conjunction, هم a mubtadaʾ and the clause يكتبون the khabar. (فَاصْبِرْ لِحُكْمِ رَبِّكَ وَلا تَكُنْ كَصاحِبِ الْحُوتِ إِذْ نادى وَهُوَ مَكْظُومٌ) the fāʾ is the faṣīḥa; اصبر is an imperative verb whose agent is latent, implied as أنت, and لحكم ربك is attached to اصبر. The wāw is a conjunction, لا prohibitive, and تكن an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by لا; its subject is latent, implied as أنت, and كصاحب الحوت is the khabar — meaning Yūnus, upon him be peace, whose story has been told before. إذ is an adverb in the accusative by an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "let not your state be like his state, nor your story like his story, at the time of his calling out". The meaning is: let there not be found in you what was found in him of vexation and leaving in anger, so that you would be tried with his trial. The clause نادى is in the position of a genitive by the adverb's being annexed to it; the wāw is circumstantial, هو a mubtadaʾ and مكظوم the khabar, and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun of نادى. (لَوْلا أَنْ تَدارَكَهُ نِعْمَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّهِ لَنُبِذَ بِالْعَراءِ وَهُوَ مَذْمُومٌ) لولا is a particle of non-occurrence because of occurrence, containing the sense of a condition; أن is a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle; تداركه is a past verb and the hāʾ a mafʿūl bihi, and نعمة is the agent; the verb was made masculine because the femininity of نعمة is not real. من ربه is a naʿt (adjective) for نعمة. أن with what falls within its scope is in the position of a nominative as a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is obligatorily omitted. The lām falls in the answer of لولا; نبذ is a passive past verb and its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent, implied as هو; بالعراء is attached to نبذ, i.e. on the open, barren land. The wāw is circumstantial, هو a mubtadaʾ and مذموم the khabar, and the clause is a ḥāl from the pronoun of نبذ. (فَاجْتَباهُ رَبُّهُ فَجَعَلَهُ مِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ) the fāʾ conjoins to something implied, i.e. "so a favour from his Lord reached him, and He chose him". اجتباه [Translator's note: the source prints «واجتباره»] is a past verb and a mafʿūl bihi, and ربه its agent, i.e. He gathered him to Himself and brought him near by accepting his repentance. فجعله is conjoined to فاجتباه; the hāʾ is the first object and من الصالحين is in the position of the second object. (وَإِنْ يَكادُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَيُزْلِقُونَكَ بِأَبْصارِهِمْ لَمَّا سَمِعُوا الذِّكْرَ) the wāw is resumptive; إن is lightened from the heavy (inna), and its subject is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), or — more likely — it is inoperative (muhmala). يكاد is an imperfect verb from the verbs of approximation, الذين its subject, and the clause كفروا the ṣila. The lām is the distinguishing lām (al-lām al-fāriqa); يزلقونك is an imperfect verb in the nominative by the retention of the nūn, the wāw is the agent and the kāf a mafʿūl bihi; بأبصارهم is attached to يزلقونك. لمّا is a linking particle or a temporal adverb (ḥīniyya ẓarfiyya); سمعوا is a verb and its agent, and الذكر a mafʿūl bihi. The meaning is that, from the intensity of their staring and casting sidelong glances at you, they almost make your foot slip, or destroy you. He said:
يتقارضون إذا التقوا في موطن ... نظرا يزل مواطىء الأقدام
(When they meet in a place they exchange looks that make the footholds of the feet slip.)
The answer of لمّا is omitted because it is indicated, i.e. "when they heard the Reminder, they almost made you slip". (وَيَقُولُونَ إِنَّهُ لَمَجْنُونٌ) the wāw is a conjunction and يقولون is conjoined to يزلقونك; إنّ and its subject, the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and مجنون its khabar; the clause is the maqūl al-qawl (object of saying) of their saying. (وَما هُوَ إِلَّا ذِكْرٌ لِلْعالَمِينَ) the wāw is circumstantial; ما is negating and inoperative because the negation is broken by إلا; هو is a mubtadaʾ, إلا a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr), ذكر the khabar of هو, and للعالمين a naʿt for ذكر.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His words «وأملي لهم إن كيدي متين» there is a non-metaphorical figure (majāz mursal): He called His granting them respite and following up favours and blessings upon them "a plot" (kayd), because it is the cause of entanglement and destruction; for the reality of plotting is a kind of stratagem, and a stratagem is to do what is outwardly beneficial and good while you intend its opposite. What came about of the ampleness of their provision, the ease of their living and the length of their lives is outwardly beneficence towards them, while what is intended by it is harm and destruction.
2- In His words «وهو مذموم» there is also a majāz mursal, because blame is in reality a cause of censure, so the relation is causality. Fine is the saying of al-Rāzī: «"And he is blameworthy", in respect of his being a doer of a sin [Translator's note: so in the source; the objection being raised is that the verse implies he committed a sin]. He said: the answer is from three aspects: first, that the word لولا indicates that this blameworthiness did not come about; second, perhaps what is meant by blameworthiness is the abandoning of what is better, for the good deeds of the righteous are the bad deeds of those brought near; third, perhaps this event was before prophethood.» Taking the verse figuratively is more fitting than straining after these possibilities.

farraa:1-1.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿نۤ وَٱلْقَلَمِ﴾.
You may conceal the final nūn or make it distinct; making it distinct is preferable to me, because it is a letter-name, and a letter-name is like something paused on even when joined. Whoever conceals it builds on the joining. The readers have read it both ways: al-Aʿmash and Ḥamza used to make it distinct, and some of them leave out the distinctness.

farraa:10-10.t: His saying: ﴿وَلاَ تُطِعْ كُلَّ حَلاَّفٍ مَّهِينٍ﴾. المهين here is the profligate. And الهماز is the one who slanders people.

farraa:11-11.t: His saying: ﴿مَّشَّآءٍ بِنَمِيمٍ﴾: نميم and نميمة (tale-bearing) are both of the speech of the Arabs.

farraa:13-13.t:
His saying: ﴿عُتُلٍّ﴾.
In this place it is the one who is fierce in quarrelling falsely. And الزنيم is the one attached to a people who is not of them, namely: the one falsely claimed [as a son] (al-daʿiyy).

farraa:14-14.t:
His saying: ﴿أَن كَانَ ذَا مَالٍ وَبَنِينَ﴾.
Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī and Abū Jaʿfar al-Madanī read it as a question: "أ أن كان", and some [read] "أن كان" with a single alif, without the question. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: ولا تُطِعْ كلَّ حَلاّفٍ مَهِينٍ أن كان: do not obey him because he is (lit. لأِنْ كان) possessed of wealth.
Whoever reads: أ أن كان ذا مال وبنين is rebuking him: Is it because he is possessed of wealth and sons that you obey him? Or if you wish, you may say: Is it because he is possessed of wealth and sons that, when Our verses are recited to him, he says: Tales of the ancients? Both are good.

farraa:16-16.t:
His saying: ﴿سَنَسِمُهُ عَلَى ٱلْخُرْطُومِ﴾.
That is: We will brand him with the brand of the people of the Fire, i.e. We will blacken his face. Even though the snout (al-khurṭūm) has been singled out for the brand, it is in the sense of the face, because part of the face stands for the rest.
The Arabs say: أما والله لأسمنّك وسماً لا يفارقك (by Allah, I will brand you with a brand that will not leave you), meaning the nose. One of them recited to me:
لأعْلِطَنَّكَ وسْماً لا يفارقه * كما يُحَزّ بِحُمىَّ المِيسمِ البَحرُ
(I will surely mark you with a brand that will not leave it, as the camel with baḥar is scored with the heat of the branding iron.)
He said "the branding iron" and did not mention the nose, because it is the place of the brand. البحر is a camel afflicted with al-baḥar, a disease that seizes camels, for which they are branded.

farraa:17-17.t:
His saying: ﴿بَلَوْنَاهُمْ﴾.
We tested the people of Mecca as We tested the owners of the garden. They were people of Yemen; one of their men had crops, date palms and vines, and he used to leave for the poor whatever of his crops the sickle missed, whatever of the palms fell onto the spread mats, and whatever of the vines the pickers missed. That used to amount to a great deal, and orphans, widows and the poor lived on it. Then the man died, leaving three sons. They said: Our father used to do that when the wealth was plentiful and the dependants few; but now that the dependants are many and the wealth is little, we will give that up. Then they conspired to harvest in the sadaf — the darkness — remaining of the night, so that nothing would be left for the poor. So Allah set a fire upon their property and burned it. They went early to their property to harvest it and saw nothing but blackness, and said: "إنا لضالُّون" (we have lost our way) — this is not our property. Then one of them said: Rather, it is our property; we have been deprived of it because of what we did to the widows and the poor. They had sworn that they would harvest it at the start of the morning, and they made no exception (lam yastathnū): they did not say "if Allah wills". So a brother of theirs, the most moderate of them, the most just of them in speech, said: Did I not say to you: why do you not glorify [Allah]? Glorifying (tasbīḥ) here has the meaning of making the exception, and it is like His saying: ﴿واذْكُرْ رَبَّكَ إِذَا نَسِيتَ﴾.

farraa:19-19.t:
His saying: ﴿فَطَافَ عَلَيْهَا طَآئِفٌ مِّن رَّبِّكَ﴾.
الطائف (a night visitant) is only by night, never by day. The Arabs have used it, saying: أطفت به نهاراً (I visited it by day), though its place is not in the daytime; but it is like your saying: لو ترك القطا ليلا لنام (if the sandgrouse were left alone at night it would sleep), because the sandgrouse does not travel by night. He said: Abū al-Jarrāḥ al-ʿUqaylī recited to me:
أطفت بها نهاراً غير ليلٍ * وألهى ربَّها طلبُ الرّخال
(I came upon it by day, not by night, while its owner was distracted by seeking the ewe-lambs.)
And الرَّخِل is the young of sheep when female.

farraa:20-20.t: His saying: ﴿فَأَصْبَحَتْ كَٱلصَّرِيمِ﴾: like the blackened night.

farraa:23-24.t:
His saying: ﴿فَٱنطَلَقُواْ وَهُمْ يَتَخَافَتُونَ﴾ ﴿أَن لاَّ يَدْخُلَنَّهَا ٱلْيَوْمَ﴾.
In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: "لا يدخلنها", without أن, because whispering is speech, and speech is quoted; so when [the verb of] saying is not overt, both أن and its omission are permissible, as Allah said: ﴿يُوصِيكُمُ اللهُ فِى أَوْلاَدِكُمْ لِلذَّكَرِ مِثْلُ حَظِّ الأُنْثَيَيْن﴾ and did not say: أنّ للذّكر; had it been so, it would have been correct.

farraa:25-25.t:
His saying: ﴿وَغَدَوْاْ عَلَىٰ حَرْدٍ قَادِرِينَ﴾.
[I.e.] with earnestness and with power in themselves [203/b]. الحرد also means purpose/direction, as a man says to another: قد أقبلت قِبلك، وقصدت قصدك، وحَرَدْتُ حَردك (I have come your way, made for your direction, headed your heading). One of them recited to me:
وجاء سيلٌ كان من أمر الله * يحرِد حَرْدَ الجنة المُغِلَّهْ
(And a flood came that was of Allah's command, heading straight for the fruitful garden.)
He means: making for it.

farraa:3-3.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإِنَّ لَكَ لأَجْراً غَيْرَ مَمْنُونٍ﴾.
[ممنون means] cut off. The Arabs say: ضعُفت مُنتى عن السفر (my strength has become too weak for travel), and a weak person is called المنين; and this is from that. And Allah knows best.

farraa:30-30.t:
His saying: ﴿فَأَقْبَلَ بَعْضُهُمْ عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍ يَتَلاَوَمُونَ﴾.
Some of them say to others: You are the one who led us and advised us to do what we did. And another says: No, you did that. That is their blaming one another.

farraa:39-39.t:
His saying: ﴿أَمْ لَكُمْ أَيْمَانٌ عَلَيْنَا بَالِغَةٌ﴾.
The readers read "بالغة" in the nominative, except al-Ḥasan, who read it in the accusative in the manner of a maṣdar (verbal noun), like your saying: حقاً (truly). البالغ is in the sense of "true": it is said جيِّد بالغ (thoroughly good), as if he said: truly good, having reached the reality of goodness. This is a good way. But what the general body [of readers] read — that البالغة is an adjective (naʿt) of الأيمان — is preferable to me, as in your saying: [do you have] oaths binding on Us that will reach with you to the Day of Resurrection, that you shall have whatever you judge? Since the lām is in the answer of إنّ, you give [إنّ] kasra. It is also said: أئن لكم ما تحكمون, as a question, and it has that same meaning, like His saying: ﴿أئذا كُنا تراباً﴾ ﴿أئنا لَمَرْدُودُونَ فِى الْحافِرَة﴾.

farraa:4-4.t: His saying: ﴿وَإِنَّكَ لَعَلَىٰ خُلُقٍ عَظِيمٍ﴾, that is: a great religion.

farraa:40-40.t:
His saying: ﴿سَلْهُمْ أَيُّهُم بِذَلِكَ زَعِيمٌ﴾.
He means: a guarantor (kafīl). He is also called الحميل, القبيل and الصبير. And الزعيم in the speech of the Arabs is the guarantor, the one who speaks for them, and the one who manages their affairs.
[Translator's note: «القائم يأمرهم» is as printed, presumably for «القائم بأمرهم» ("the one who manages their affairs").]

farraa:41-41.t:
His saying: ﴿أَمْ لَهُمْ شُرَكَآءُ فَلْيَأتُواْ بِشُرَكَآئِهِمْ﴾.
In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: "أم لهم شرك فليأتوا بشركهم". شِرك and شركاء have one meaning: you say: فى هذا الأمر شِرْك (in this matter there are partners) and فيه شركاء.

farraa:42-42.t:
His saying: ﴿يَوْمَ يُكْشَفُ عَن سَاقٍ﴾.
The readers are agreed on ḍamma on the yāʾ. [Muḥammad told us,] he said: al-Farrāʾ told us, he said: Sufyān told me, from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he read: "يوم تكشف عن ساق", meaning the Resurrection and the Hour, because of its severity. He said: and one of the Arabs recited to me, by the grandfather of Abū Ṭarafa:
كشفَتْ لهم عن ساقها * وبدا من الشرِّ البراحُ
(It [war] bared its shin to them, and the evil became plainly manifest.)

farraa:44-44.t:
His saying: ﴿فَذَرْنِي وَمَن يُكَذِّبُ بِهَـٰذَا ٱلْحَدِيثِ﴾.
The meaning of "leave Me and whoever denies" is: entrust them to Me. You say to a man: لو تركتك ورأيك ما أفلحت (had I left you to your own judgement, you would not have prospered), i.e.: had I entrusted you to your judgement, you would not have prospered. Likewise His saying: ﴿ذَرْنِى وَمَنْ خَلَقْتُ وحِيداً﴾. (من) is in the position of the accusative. When you say: قد تُرِكتَ ورأيَك and خُليت ورأيك (you have been left to your judgement), you put الرأى in the accusative, because the meaning is: you were left to your judgement; so you make the second accusative because this meaning suits it, and because the noun before it is attached to a verb.
But when the Arabs say: لو تركت أنت ورأيُكَ, they make it nominative because of the strength of أنت, since it is overt and not attached to the verb.
Likewise they say: لو ترك عبدالله والأسدُ لأكله (if ʿAbd Allāh and the lion were left together, it would eat him). If they use a pronoun for ʿAbd Allāh and say: لو ترك والأسدَ أكله, they put [الأسد] in the accusative, because the noun is not overt. If they say: لو ترك هو والأسد, they prefer the nominative in الأسد. What is permissible in the one is permissible in the other, except that the speech of [204/a] the Arabs is as I have informed you — except for their saying: قد ترك بعضُ القوم وبعض (some of the people were left with others), where they prefer agreement (itbāʿ), because بعض and بعض, since they agree in meaning and name, agreement was chosen for them; yet the accusative in the second is not ruled out.

farraa:47-47.t:
His saying: ﴿أَمْ عِندَهُمُ ٱلْغَيْبُ فَهُمْ يَكْتُبُونَ﴾.
He is saying: Do they have the Preserved Tablet, so that they write from it and dispute with you by it?

farraa:48-48.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلاَ تَكُن كَصَاحِبِ ٱلْحُوتِ﴾.
[I.e.] like Jonah ﷺ. He is saying: do not become exasperated with them as Jonah became exasperated, so that he fled from his people and cast himself into the sea, until the fish swallowed him.

farraa:49-50.t:
His saying: ﴿لَّوْلاَ أَن تَدَارَكَهُ نِعْمَةٌ مِّن رَّبِّهِ لَنُبِذَ بِٱلْعَرَآءِ﴾.
[I.e., he would have been cast out] at the time he was cast out while blameworthy; but he was cast out not blameworthy. ﴿فَٱجْتَبَاهُ رَبُّهُ﴾.
In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: "لولا أن تداركته". That is like His saying: ﴿وَأخَذَ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا الصَّيْحَةُ﴾ and ﴿وأخذت﴾ in another place, because نعمة is a feminine noun derived from a verb, and when its verb comes first you may make it masculine or feminine.
His saying: ﴿لَنُبِذَ بِٱلْعَرَآءِ﴾. العراء is the [bare] land.
[Muḥammad ibn al-Jahm told us, he said: al-Farrāʾ told us.]
[Translator's note: «نبد عير مذموم» is as printed, for «نُبذ غيرَ مذموم».]

farraa:5-6.t:
His saying: ﴿فَسَتُبْصِرُ وَيُبْصِرُونَ﴾ ﴿بِأَيِّكُمُ ٱلْمَفْتُونُ﴾.
المفتون here has the meaning of madness (al-junūn): it is in the manner of [the maṣdar] الفتون, as they said: ليس له معقول رأى (he has no sound judgement), [using a passive-participle form as a maṣdar]. And if you wish, you may take بأيكم as فى أيكم, i.e.: in which of the two parties is the madman; it is then a noun, not a maṣdar.

farraa:51-52.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإِن يَكَادُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ لَيُزْلِقُونَكَ بِأَبْصَارِهِمْ﴾.
ʿĀṣim and al-Aʿmash read it: (ليُزلِقونك) with ḍamma on the yāʾ, from أزلقتُ; and the people of Medina read it: (ليَزلقونك) with fatḥa on the yāʾ, from زَلَقْتُ. The Arabs say of one who shaves the head: قد زلقه and أزلقه. Ibn ʿAbbās read it: "ليُزْهقونك بأبصارهم". Muḥammad told us, he said: I heard al-Farrāʾ say: Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna told us that, from a man, [from] Ibn ʿAbbās. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd it is likewise with hāʾ: "ليزهقونك", i.e.: they would strike you down with their eyes. That is because when one of the Arabs wanted to put the evil eye on property — i.e. to strike it with the eye — he would starve himself for three days, then confront that property and say: By Allah, [I have never seen] property more abundant or finer [meaning: I have not seen more abundant], and camels would fall down from it. They wanted to do the like with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and said: We have never seen the like of his arguments; and they looked at him to strike him with the eye, and said: We have never seen the like of him, and he is surely mad. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿وَمَا هُوَ إِلاَّ ذِكْرٌ لِّلْعَالَمِينَ﴾. It is also said: (وإن كادوا ليزلقونك), i.e.: they would hurl you from your place and remove you from it with their eyes, as you say: كاد يصرعنى بشدة نظره (he almost felled me with the intensity of his gaze); this is clear and frequent in the speech of the Arabs, as you say: أزهقت السهم فزهق (I sent the arrow flying and it went).
[Translator's note: «عن رجل ابن عباس» is as printed; a «عن» seems to have dropped out before «ابن عباس». The printed text also has «فرهق», translated as «فزهق».]

farraa:9-9.t:
His saying: ﴿وَدُّواْ لَوْ تُدْهِنُ﴾.
It is said: they wished that you would be pliant in your religion, so that they would be pliant in theirs. And some said: that you would disbelieve, so that they would disbelieve, i.e.: so that they would follow you in disbelief.
[Translator's note: «لو تفكر فيكفرون» is as printed, evidently for «لو تكفر فيكفرون».]

harrat-mujtaba:1-1.t: «ن» is a particle with no grammatical position; «والقلم» is the thing sworn by, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied verb «أقسم» (I swear); «ما» is a nominal relative conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «القلم», i.e.: and what they inscribe.

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: The clause (ما أنت بمجنون) is the answer to the oath; «ما» is negative, acting like ليس, and the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida) in its khabar (predicate), which is «مجنون»; the preposition phrase «بنعمة» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «مجنون», the implied form being: you are not mad, being clothed in a blessing.

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: The clause «وإن لك لأجرا» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «ما أنت بمجنون»; the lām is for emphasis; «غير» is a naʿt (adjective).

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: The clause «فستبصر» is resumptive; the verb here is suspended from governing by the interrogative after it.

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: «بأييكم» is a preposition and its genitive noun; the bāʾ has the meaning of (في), attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) «المفتون», i.e.: in which group of you is the one afflicted; the clause «بأييكم المفتون» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the verb of seeing, suspended by the interrogative.

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: The clause «هو أعلم» is the khabar (predicate) of «إن»; «بمن» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أعلم»; the second clause «وهو أعلم» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the first; the preposition phrase «بالمهتدين» is attached to «أعلم».

harrat-mujtaba:9-9.t: The clause «ودُّوا» is parenthetical; «لو» is maṣdariyya (infinitival), and the maṣdar (verbal noun) is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause «فيدهنون» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «تدهن».

harrat-mujtaba:10-10.t: The clause «ولا تُطع» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «لا تطع» in verse (8).

harrat-mujtaba:11-11.t: «همَّاز» is a second naʿt (adjective) of {حَلافٍ}, and likewise «مشَّاء»; the preposition phrase is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «مشَّاء».

harrat-mujtaba:12-12.t: «منَّاع» is a naʿt (adjective) of {حَلافٍ}; «للخير»: the lām is redundant (zāʾida), for strengthening, and «الخير» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of «منَّاع»; «معتد» is another naʿt of {حَلافٍ}, and likewise «أثيم».

harrat-mujtaba:14-14.t: The maṣdar (verbal noun) «أن كان» is genitive by an implied (muqaddar) lām attached to (mutaʿalliq) the preceding verb of prohibition, i.e.: do not obey one whose attributes are these, because he was wealthy and possessed of sons.

harrat-mujtaba:15-15.t: The conditional clause is a second khabar (predicate) of {كَانَ}; «أساطير» is the khabar of an implied (muqaddar) mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e.: they are legends (هي أساطير); and the clause «تتلى» is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

harrat-mujtaba:17-17.t: The kāf is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), and «ما» is maṣdariyya (infinitival), i.e.: We tried them with a trial like Our trial of the owners of the garden; «إذ» is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أقسموا»; the clause «ليصرمنَّها» is the answer to the oath; «مصبحين» is from the complete (tāmm) «أصبح», and it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «ليصرمنَّها», i.e.: entering upon the morning; the verb is an imperfect, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, which was omitted because of a succession of identical letters; the wāw, omitted because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, is the fāʿil, and the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

harrat-mujtaba:18-18.t: (ولا يستثنون) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:19-19.t: The clause «فطاف» is resumptive; the preposition phrase «من ربك» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «طائف»; the clause «وهم نائمون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause.

harrat-mujtaba:20-20.t: The clause «فأصبحت» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «طاف».

harrat-mujtaba:21-21.t: The clause «فتنادوا» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «أصبحت»; «مصبحين» is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

harrat-mujtaba:22-22.t: «أن» is explicative (tafsīriyya), and the clause after it is explanatory; the conditional clause is resumptive, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, what precedes indicating it.

harrat-mujtaba:23-23.t: The clause «فانطلقوا» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «تنادَوا», and the clause «وهم يتخافتون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause.

harrat-mujtaba:24-24.t: «أن» is explicative (tafsīriyya), and «مسكين» is the fāʿil (agent).

harrat-mujtaba:25-25.t: The wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); the clause «غدوا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause from the fāʿil (agent) of {يَتَخَافَتُونَ}; it is an abrogating (nāsikh) past verb with its noun and its khabar (predicate); the preposition phrase is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «قادرين».

harrat-mujtaba:26-26.t: The fāʾ is resumptive; the conditional clause is resumptive; the clause «قالوا» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ).

harrat-mujtaba:27-27.t: (بل نحن محرومون) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:29-29.t: «سبحان» is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), and the clause «إنَّا كنَّا» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:30-30.t: The clause «فأقبل» is resumptive, and the clause «يتلاومون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «بعضهم».

harrat-mujtaba:32-32.t: The maṣdar (verbal noun) is the khabar (predicate) of «عسى»; «خيرا» is a second object; the preposition phrase «منها» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «خيرا»; the clause «إنَّا راغبون» is resumptive, and the preposition phrase is attached to «راغبون».

harrat-mujtaba:33-33.t: (كذلك العذاب) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The preposition phrase is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of «العذاب»; the clause «ولَعذاب الآخرة أكبر» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the resumptive clause; the conditional clause is resumptive, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, its implied form being: they would have obeyed us (أطاعونا).

harrat-mujtaba:34-34.t: The adverb «عند» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the [notion of] being-settled (al-istiqrār) to which the khabar (predicate) is attached.

harrat-mujtaba:35-35.t: (أفنجعل المسلمين كالمجرمين) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive, and the kāf is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the second object.

harrat-mujtaba:36-36.t: «ما» is an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ (subject); the preposition phrase «لكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate); «كيف» is an interrogative noun, a ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause «تحكمون» is a badal (substitute) from the clause «ما لكم».

harrat-mujtaba:37-37.t: «أم» is the disjunctive [one] (al-munqaṭiʿa); the clause «تدرسون» is a naʿt (adjective) of «كتاب»; the preposition phrase «فيه» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «تدرسون».

harrat-mujtaba:38-38.t: The preposition phrase «فيه» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the [notion of] being-settled (al-istiqrār) to which the khabar (predicate) is attached; the lām is for emphasis; «ما» is a relative noun, the noun of «إن»; the clause «إن لكم فيه لما تخيرون» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of {تَدْرُسُونَ}, i.e.: you study in it that you have …; when the lām entered, the hamza took kasra.

harrat-mujtaba:39-39.t: «أم» is the disjunctive [one] (al-munqaṭiʿa); the preposition phrase «علينا» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «أيمان»; the preposition phrase «إلى يوم» is attached to the [notion of] being-settled (al-istiqrār) to which the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) «أيمان» is attached; the lām in «لما» is for emphasis; the preposition phrase «لكم» is attached to the khabar of «إن», whose noun is «ما»; and the clause «إن لكم لما تحكمون» is the answer to the oath contained in his words «أيمان».

harrat-mujtaba:40-40.t: «أيهم» is an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «زعيم» is its khabar (predicate); the preposition phrase «بذلك» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «زعيم»; the clause (أيهم زعيم) is the second object of the asking, suspended by the interrogative; «سأل» is suspended because it is a means to knowledge.

harrat-mujtaba:41-41.t: «أم» is the disjunctive [one] (al-munqaṭiʿa); the clause «فليأتوا» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «لهم شركاء»; the conditional clause is resumptive, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, what precedes indicating it.

harrat-mujtaba:42-42.t: The adverb «يوم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) his words {فَلْيَأْتُوا}; the clause «يكشف» is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause «فلا يستطيعون» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «يُدْعون».

harrat-mujtaba:43-43.t: «خاشعة» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «يُدْعَوْن»; «أبصارهم» is the fāʿil (agent) of «خاشعة»; the clause «ترهقهم» is a ḥāl from the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) in «يُدْعَون»; the clause «وقد كانوا» is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «ترهقهم»; the clause «وهم سالمون» is a ḥāl from the wāw in «يدعون».

harrat-mujtaba:44-44.t: The clause «فَذَرْني» is resumptive; the relative noun is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the yāʾ in «ذرني»; the clause «سنستدرجهم» is resumptive; and the clause «لا يعلمون» is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

harrat-mujtaba:45-45.t: The clause «وأملي» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause {سَنَسْتَدْرِجُهُمْ}, and the clause «إن كيدي متين» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:46-46.t: «أم» is disjunctive (munqaṭiʿa); the clause «فهم مثقلون» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «تسألهم»; the preposition phrase «مِنْ مغرم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «مثقلون».

harrat-mujtaba:47-47.t: The clause «فهم يكتبون» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «عندهم الغيب».

harrat-mujtaba:48-48.t: The clause «فاصبر» is resumptive; «إذ» is an adverbial noun, a badal (substitute) of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) from «صاحب الحوت»; the clause «وهو مكظوم» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause from the pronoun in «نادى».

harrat-mujtaba:49-49.t: The conditional clause is resumptive; «لولا» is a particle of impossibility-upon-impossibility [i.e. "were it not for"]; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being "موجود" (existing); the preposition phrase «من ربه» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «نعمة»; the clause «وهو مذموم» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause from the pronoun in «نبذ».

harrat-mujtaba:50-50.t: The clause «فاجتباه» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the preceding conditional clause; the preposition phrase «من الصالحين» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted second object.

harrat-mujtaba:51-51.t: The clause «وإن يكاد» is resumptive; «إنْ» is lightened and inoperative (muhmala), and the lām after it is the distinguishing lām (al-lām al-fāriqa); the conditional clause is parenthetical, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, what precedes indicating it, i.e.: they almost made you slip; the clause «ويقولون» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «يزلقونك».

harrat-mujtaba:52-52.t: The clause «وما هو إلا ذكر» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause, and «إلا» is for restriction (ḥaṣr); the preposition phrase «للعالمين» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «ذكر».

mekki-muskil:44-44.t: His saying (فذرني ومن يكذب): (من) is in the position of the accusative (naṣb) by conjunction with the pronoun of the speaker; or, if you wish, as a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment).

mekki-muskil:49-49.t:
His saying (لولا أن تداركه): (أن) is in the position of the nominative (rafʿ) as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is omitted; according to Sībawayh it is hardly ever used with (لولا) except omitted. The implied meaning is: "Were it not for Allah's overtaking him, it would have caught him" or "rescued him", or the like. (لنبذ) is the answer (jawāb) of (لولا). (تداركه) is masculine because (النعمة) and (النعم) have one meaning, so it is construed according to the meaning. It is also said that it is masculine because a separation stands between them, namely the hāʾ [Translator's note: i.e. the object pronoun of تداركه separates the verb from its agent]. It is also said: because the femininity of (النعمة) is not real, since it has no masculine from its own word. In the reading of Ibn Masʿūd: (لولا أن تداركته), with tāʾ, treating the word as feminine.
His saying (وهو مذموم): a mubtadaʾ and khabar, in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the nominative pronoun in (نبذ).

mekki-muskil:51-51.t: His saying (وإن يكاد الذين كفروا ليزلقونك): according to the Kufans, (إن) means (ما) and the lām means (إلا); the implied form is: "And those who disbelieve almost do nothing but make you slip". According to the Basrans, (إن) is lightened from the heavy (إنّ), its noun is implied with it, and the lām is the lām of emphasis, which is obligatory in this kind so that it does not resemble the (إن) that means (ما). Its like has already been discussed.

mekki-muskil:1-1.t: His saying, Exalted is He, نون والقلم: the justification of pronouncing the nūn clearly (iẓhār) and of assimilating it (idghām) has preceded in [Sūrat] Yā Sīn and elsewhere. It has been read with a fatḥa on the nūn, on the basis that it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. "mention Nūn" or "recite Nūn"; it is a diptote because it is definite and the name of something feminine, namely the sūra; it is also said: because it is a foreign noun. Sībawayh said the nūn was given a fatḥa only because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, like أين and كيف, as if the reader connected his recitation and did not assimilate, so two quiescent letters came together, the nūn and the wāw, and the nūn was given a fatḥa. Al-Farrāʾ said it was given a fatḥa only by likening it to ثمّ. Others said it was given a fatḥa because it resembled the nūn of the plural. Abū Ḥātim said: when the wāw of the oath was omitted from it, it was made accusative by the verb of swearing, as you say اللهَ لأفعلن ("By Allah, I will surely do it"), making the noun accusative by the verb, as if in the representation [it were "I swear by Allah"], even though أقسم الله is not used. Sībawayh permitted اللهِ لأفعلن in the genitive, making the particle of the oath govern although it is omitted; that was permissible in this, though not permissible elsewhere, because of the frequent use of omission in the chapter of the oath. Whoever makes نون an oath makes the answer [to it] ما أنت بنعمة ربك.

mekki-muskil:14-14.t: His saying أَن كَانَ ذَا مَال: أن is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), and the governing word in it is an implied verb, its implied form being "he disbelieves" or "he denies, because he has wealth". It is not permissible for the governing word to be تتلى nor قال, because what comes after إذا does not govern what precedes it, since إذا is annexed to the clauses after it, and the muḍāf ilayhi does not govern what precedes the muḍāf; and قال is the apodosis of the conditional, and it does not govern what precedes the conditional, because the rule of the governor is to come before what it governs, and the rule of the apodosis is to come after the condition, so it would become fronted and postponed at the same time, and that is not permissible. So a governing word must be implied, because of what we mentioned.

mekki-muskil:17-17.t:
His saying مصبحين: a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the nominative latent pronoun in ليصرمنها; أصبح has no khabar (predicate) in this, because it means "entering upon the morning".
His saying بأيكم الْمفْتُون: the بـ [is redundant], and the meaning is "which of you is the afflicted one" (أيكم المفتون). [Translator's note: a word appears to have dropped after «الباء» in the edition; the following clause («It is also said that the بـ is not redundant») shows that «زائدة» ("redundant") is meant.] It is also said that the بـ is not redundant, but it has the meaning of في; and it is also said that المفتون means الفتون (affliction), the implied form being "in which of you is the affliction", i.e. madness.
أيكم was written in the Muṣḥaf in this place specifically with two yāʾs and an alif before them. The reason for that is that they wrote the hamza with a form according to its full pronunciation (taḥqīq) and a form according to its lightening (takhfīf): the alif is the form of the hamza according to full pronunciation, and the first yāʾ is its form according to lightening, because before the hamza there is a kasra, so when you lighten it, its rule is to be replaced by a yāʾ; and the second yāʾ is the form of the doubled yāʾ. Likewise they wrote بأييد with two yāʾs for this reason; and they wrote ولأاوضعوا with two alifs, and likewise أو لأاذبحنه, ولا إلى الجحيم and لا إلى الله تحشرون — all of it was written with two alifs, one of which, the first, is the form of the hamza according to full pronunciation, and the second its form according to lightening. It has also been said that the first is the form of the hamza and the second the form of its vowel; and it is also said that it is a fatḥa that was prolonged and an alif was generated from it, and there is remoteness in that. This is only a justification of the script of the Muṣḥaf, since it has come that way and there is no way to alter it. This chapter is wide, and it is frequent in the script, departing from the script customary among scribes, so a justification befitting it must be drawn out. We will mention it, if Allah the Exalted wills, exhaustively and with its reasons, in a work other than this. [Translator's note: the edition prints «أذبخنه» and «وَلَا الى الْجَحِيم»; they are rendered here as the intended Muṣḥaf spellings with two alifs.]
His saying قَالَ أساطير الْأَوَّلين: i.e. "these are legends" (هذه أساطير), so أساطير is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject).

mekki-muskil:33-33.t:
His saying كَذَلِك الْعَذَاب: العذاب is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and كذلك the khabar (predicate), i.e. the punishment that befalls the disbelievers is like this punishment.
His saying مَا لكم كَيفَ تحكمون: ما is an interrogative mubtadaʾ, لكم the khabar, and كيف is in the position of the accusative by تحكمون.

mekki-muskil:39-39.t: His saying أم لكم أَيْمَان علينا بالغه: أيمان is a mubtadaʾ (subject), علينا the khabar (predicate), and بالغة a naʿt (adjective) of أيمان. Al-Ḥasan read بالغةً in the accusative, as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the nominative latent pronoun in علينا.

mekki-muskil:42-42.t: His saying يَوْم يكْشف: يوم is accusative by [an implied] "remember, O Muhammad" (اذكر يا محمد), so you begin with it. It is also possible that يأتوا makes it accusative, i.e. "let them bring their partners on this day"; then beginning with it is not good.

mekki-muskil:43-43.t: His saying خاشعة أَبْصَارهم: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the latent pronoun in يدعون or of the latent pronoun in يستطيعون; أبصارهم is nominative by its verb [i.e. by خاشعة as its agent]. ترهقهم is in the position of a ḥāl like the first; if you wish, it may be detached from the first [i.e. a new sentence].

muyesser-irab:1-1.t:
﴿ن﴾: the discussion of the disconnected letters (al-ḥurūf al-muqaṭṭaʿa) has preceded at the beginning of Sūrat al-Baqara.
﴿والقلم﴾: the wāw is a particle of oath and of the genitive; «القلم» is that by which the oath is sworn (muqsam bihi); the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb, its implied form being «أقسم» (I swear).
﴿وما﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; «ما» is relative or maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya); in either case it is conjoined to «القلم».
﴿يسطرون﴾: a verb and its fāʿil (agent); the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) is omitted; the clause ﴿يسطرون﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:2-2.t:
﴿ما﴾: the Ḥijāzī negating [«ما»], which governs as «ليس» does.
﴿أنت﴾: an indeclinable (mabnī) pronoun in the position of a nominative (marfūʿ) as the noun of ﴿ما﴾.
﴿بنعمة﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the content of the negated clause, the bāʾ thus being causal (sababiyya).
﴿ربك﴾: a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿بمجنون﴾: the bāʾ is a redundant (ṣila) preposition, and ﴿مجنون﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of the Ḥijāzī ﴿ما﴾, accusative in position and made genitive (majrūr) in form by the bāʾ; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the answer to the oath.

muyesser-irab:3-3.t:
﴿وإن﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and the clause with what follows it is conjoined to the clause that answers the oath; «إن» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh).
﴿لك﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the fronted khabar (predicate) of «إن».
﴿لأجرا﴾: the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and «أجرًا» is the noun of «إن».
﴿غير﴾: a naʿt (adjective).
﴿ممنون﴾: a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

muyesser-irab:4-4.t:
﴿وإنك﴾: «إن» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and the kāf is its noun.
﴿لعلى خلق﴾: the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); «على خلق» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate).
﴿عظيم﴾: a naʿt (adjective).

muyesser-irab:5-5.t:
﴿فستبصر﴾: the fāʾ is «استثنائية» (exceptive) «[Translator's note: so in the source; probably a slip for «استئنافية» (resumptive).]»; the sīn is a particle of the future; «تبصر» is an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being «أنت» (you).
﴿ويبصرون﴾: conjoined to ﴿ستبصر﴾.

muyesser-irab:6-6.t:
﴿بأيكم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); «أي» is an interrogative noun, and «كم» is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿المفتون﴾: a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), in the nominative (marfūʿ); the clause is in the position of an accusative (manṣūb) as the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of ﴿تبصر﴾.

muyesser-irab:7-7.t:
﴿إن ربك﴾: «إن» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh); «رب» is its noun, and the kāf is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿هو﴾: a mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿أعلم﴾: the khabar (predicate), and the clause is the khabar of «إن». Or ﴿هو﴾ is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl), and «أعلم» is the khabar of «إن».
﴿بمن﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أعلم﴾.
﴿ضل﴾: an indeclinable (mabnī) past verb, the fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir); the clause ﴿ضل﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.
﴿عن سبيله﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿ضل﴾; the clause has no grammatical position, because it gives the reason (taʿlīl) for what precedes.
﴿وهو﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «هو» is a mubtadaʾ.
﴿أعلم﴾: the khabar.
﴿بالمهتدين﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أعلم﴾.

muyesser-irab:8-8.t:
﴿فلا﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition), because it conjoins to an omitted [clause] indicated by the context; «لا» is prohibitive.
﴿تطع﴾: an imperfect verb made jussive (majzūm) by «لا»; the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being «أنت» (you).
﴿المكذبين﴾: a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

muyesser-irab:9-9.t:
﴿ودوا﴾: a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma because it is joined to the wāw of the plural.
﴿لو﴾: maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya).
﴿تدهن﴾: an imperfect verb, the fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir).
﴿فيدهنون﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; «يدهنون» is an imperfect verb, conjoined to «تدهن», so it falls within the scope of «لو» and is part of what is wished for; what is wished for is two things, the second of them caused by the first. Or it is the khabar (predicate) of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e.: «فهم مدهنون» (so they would be compromising).

muyesser-irab:10-10.t:
﴿ولا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «لا» is prohibitive.
﴿تطع﴾: an imperfect verb made jussive (majzūm) by «لا».
﴿كل﴾: a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿حلاف﴾: a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿مهين﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿حلاف﴾.

muyesser-irab:11-11.t:
﴿هماز مشاء﴾: two adjectives (ṣifa) of ﴿حلاف﴾, made genitive (majrūr) by the kasra.
﴿بنميم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿مشاء﴾.

muyesser-irab:12-12.t:
﴿مناع﴾: an adjective (ṣifa) of ﴿حلاف﴾, made genitive (majrūr) by the kasra.
﴿للخير﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿مناع﴾.
﴿معتد أثيم﴾: likewise two adjectives of ﴿حلاف﴾.

muyesser-irab:13-13.t:
﴿عتل﴾: an adjective (ṣifa) of ﴿حلاف﴾, made genitive (majrūr) by the kasra.
﴿بعد﴾: an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿زنيم﴾.
﴿ذلك﴾: a demonstrative in the position of a genitive as a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿زنيم﴾: an adjective of ﴿حلاف﴾, made genitive by the kasra.

muyesser-irab:14-14.t:
﴿أن﴾: maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya); it, together with what falls within its scope, is in the place of an accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e.: «لأن كان» (because he was); and it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) what «إذا تتلى» indicates, i.e.: he denied them. It is not valid for it to be governed by the verb of the protasis, because «إذا» is annexed to the clause after it, and the muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) does not govern what precedes the muḍāf; nor is it valid for it to be governed by «قال», which is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), because what comes after the conditional particle does not govern what precedes it.
﴿كان﴾: a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb; its noun is latent (mustatir), its implied form being «هم» (they) «[Translator's note: so in the source; the latent pronoun is singular, «هو» (he).]».
﴿ذا﴾: its khabar (predicate).
﴿مال﴾: a muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿وبنين﴾: conjoined to «مال».

muyesser-irab:15-15.t:
﴿إذا﴾: an adverb of future time containing the meaning of condition; it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) its apodosis (jawāb).
﴿تتلى﴾: an imperfect verb built for the one whose agent is not named (passive).
﴿عليه﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿تتلى﴾; the clause is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by the annexation of the adverb to it.
﴿آياتنا﴾: the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), made nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma, and ﴿نا﴾ is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿قال﴾: a past verb, the fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir); the clause «قال» has no grammatical position, because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
﴿أساطير﴾: the khabar (predicate) of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e.: «هي أساطير» (they are tales).
﴿الأولين﴾: a muḍāf ilayhi.

muyesser-irab:16-16.t:
﴿سنسمه﴾: a resumptive clause with no grammatical position; the sīn is a particle of the future; «نسمه» is an imperfect verb with a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent), and the hāʾ is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿على الخرطوم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿نسمه﴾.

muyesser-irab:17-17.t:
﴿إنا﴾: «إن» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and ﴿نا﴾ is its noun.
﴿بلوناهم﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its object; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of «إن».
﴿كما﴾: the kāf is a noun in the sense of «مثل» (like), indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, in the position of an accusative (manṣūb) as an adjective (ṣifa) of an omitted maṣdar, i.e.: «مثل ما بلونا» (like what We tried); ﴿ما﴾ is maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya); ﴿بلونا﴾ is a past verb and ﴿نا﴾ is the fāʿil; and the interpreted maṣdar from ﴿ما﴾ and the verb is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿بلونا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil.
﴿أصحاب﴾: a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿الجنة﴾: a muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿إذ﴾: an adverb of past time, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿بلونا﴾.
﴿أقسموا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by the annexation of the adverb to it.
﴿ليصرمنها﴾: the lām occurs in the answer to the oath; «يصرمنها» is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, which was dropped because of the succession of like letters; the wāw, dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, is the fāʿil, i.e.: «ليصرموننها».
﴿مصبحين﴾: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil of ﴿ليصرمنها﴾; it is an active participle of the complete (tāmma) «أصبح».

muyesser-irab:18-18.t:
﴿ولا﴾: the wāw is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya) or circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and «لا» is the negating one.
﴿يستثنون﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, because it is one of the five verbs (al-afʿāl al-khamsa); the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the clause ﴿ولا يستثنون﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position, or circumstantial, in the position of an accusative (manṣūb).

muyesser-irab:19-19.t:
﴿فطاف﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and «طاف» is a past verb.
﴿عليها﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿طاف﴾.
﴿طائف﴾: the fāʿil (agent).
﴿من ربك﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of ﴿طائف﴾.
﴿وهم﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and «هم» is a mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿نائمون﴾: the khabar (predicate), made nominative (marfūʿ) by the wāw.

muyesser-irab:20-20.t:
﴿فأصبحت﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; «أصبحت» is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, its noun being latent (mustatir), its implied form being «هي» (it).
﴿كالصريم﴾: the kāf is a noun in the sense of «مثل» (like), indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, in the position of an accusative (manṣūb) as the khabar (predicate) of ﴿أصبح﴾, and ﴿الصريم﴾ is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

muyesser-irab:21-21.t:
﴿فتنادوا﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; «تنادوا» is a past verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent).
﴿مصبحين﴾: a ḥāl (circumstantial), made accusative (manṣūb) by the yāʾ, because it is a sound masculine plural.

muyesser-irab:22-22.t:
﴿أن﴾: explicative (tafsīriyya).
﴿اغدوا﴾: a defective (nāqiṣ) imperative verb, and the wāw is its noun.
﴿على حرثكم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿اغدوا﴾. The clause ﴿اغدوا...﴾ is explicative, with no grammatical position.
﴿إن﴾: conditional.
﴿كنتم﴾: a defective past verb in the position of a jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the tāʾ is the noun of «كان».
﴿صارمين﴾: the khabar (predicate) of «كان», made accusative (manṣūb) by the yāʾ; the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, i.e.: «إن كنتم صارمين فاغدوا» (if you would harvest, then go early).

muyesser-irab:23-23.t:
﴿فانطلقوا﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; «انطلقوا» is a past verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent).
﴿وهم﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and «هم» is a mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿يتخافتون﴾: an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause ﴿يتخافتون﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, and the clause ﴿وهم يتخافتون﴾ is in the position of an accusative (manṣūb) as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

muyesser-irab:24-24.t:
﴿أن﴾: explicative (tafsīriyya), because whispering contains the meaning of saying without its letters; the clause after it is explicative, with no grammatical position.
﴿لا﴾: prohibitive.
﴿يدخلنها﴾: an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa because it is joined to the heavy nūn of emphasis, in the position of a jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive «لا»; ﴿ها﴾ is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) by extension (ʿalā al-saʿa).
﴿اليوم﴾: an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يدخلنها﴾.
﴿عليكم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, also attached to ﴿يدخلنها﴾.
﴿مسكين﴾: the fāʿil (agent).

muyesser-irab:25-25.t:
﴿وغدوا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; «غدوا» is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, and the wāw is its noun.
﴿على حرد﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿قادرين﴾.
﴿قادرين﴾: the khabar (predicate) of «غدوا». Or «غدوا» is complete (tāmma), and «قادرين» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «غدوا», with ﴿على حرد﴾ attached to it. Or ﴿على حرد﴾ is the ḥāl, and «قادرين» is a second ḥāl, or a ḥāl from the pronoun of the first ḥāl, so that it is an overlapping ḥāl (ḥāl mutadākhila).

muyesser-irab:26-26.t:
﴿فلما﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and «لما» is temporal (ḥīniyya), or linking.
﴿رأوها﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by the annexation of the adverb to it.
﴿قالوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause has no grammatical position, because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
﴿إنا﴾: «إن» [and] its noun «[Translator's note: so worded in the source: «إن اسمها»; i.e. «إنّ» is an abrogating particle and «نا» is its noun.]».
﴿لضالون﴾: the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and «ضالون» is the khabar (predicate) of «إن»; «إن», its noun and its khabar are the maqūl al-qawl (object of saying).

muyesser-irab:27-27.t:
﴿بل﴾: a particle of digression (iḍrāb) and conjunction.
﴿نحن﴾: an indeclinable (mabnī) pronoun in the position of a nominative (marfūʿ) as a mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿محرومون﴾: the khabar (predicate), made nominative by the wāw.

muyesser-irab:28-28.t:
﴿قال﴾: a past verb.
﴿أوسطهم﴾: the fāʿil (agent).
﴿ألم﴾: the hamza is for the interrogative of disavowal (al-istifhām al-inkārī), and «لم» is a particle of negation, of conversion [to the past] and of the jussive.
﴿أقل﴾: an imperfect verb made jussive (majzūm) by ﴿لم﴾.
﴿لكم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أقل﴾.
﴿لولا﴾: a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ), i.e.: «هلّا» (why not).
﴿تسبحون﴾: an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; its object is omitted, i.e. the Name of Majesty.

muyesser-irab:29-29.t:
﴿قالوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent).
﴿سبحان﴾: it stands in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), made accusative (manṣūb) by an omitted verb.
﴿ربنا﴾: a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿إنا﴾: «إن» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and ﴿نا﴾ is its noun.
﴿كنّا﴾: «كان» is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, and ﴿نا﴾ is its noun.
﴿ظالمين﴾: the khabar (predicate) of «كان»; the clause ﴿كنا ظالمين﴾ is the khabar of «إن», and the clause «إنّا كنّا» gives the reason (taʿlīliyya).

muyesser-irab:30-30.t:
﴿فأقبل﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and «أقبل» is a past verb.
﴿بعضهم﴾: the fāʿil (agent).
﴿على بعض﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أقبل﴾.
﴿يتلاومون﴾: an imperfect verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

muyesser-irab:31-31.t:
﴿قالوا﴾: a past verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent).
﴿يا﴾: a vocative particle.
﴿ويلنا﴾: the one addressed (munādā), a muḍāf, in the accusative (manṣūb).
﴿إنا﴾: «إن» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and ﴿نا﴾ is its noun.
﴿كنّا﴾: «كان» is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, and ﴿نا﴾ is its noun.
﴿طاغين﴾: the khabar (predicate) of «كان»; the clause ﴿كنا طاغين﴾ is the khabar of «إن».

muyesser-irab:32-32.t:
﴿عسى﴾: a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, one of the verbs of hope (afʿāl al-rajāʾ).
﴿ربنا﴾: the noun of «عسى».
﴿أن﴾: an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh) that makes the noun accusative and the khabar nominative «[Translator's note: so in the source; «أن» here is the maṣdar-forming particle that makes the imperfect verb accusative, as the next line indicates.]».
﴿يبدلنا﴾: an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb); the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), and ﴿نا﴾ is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); «أن» together with what falls within its scope is the khabar (predicate) of «عسى».
﴿خيرًا﴾: a second mafʿūl bihi.
﴿منها﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿خيرًا﴾.
﴿إنا﴾: «إن» is an abrogating particle, and ﴿نا﴾ is its noun.
﴿إلى ربنا﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿راغبون﴾.
﴿راغبون﴾: the khabar of «إنّ».

muyesser-irab:33-33.t:
﴿كذلك﴾: the kāf is a noun in the sense of «مثل» (like), indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, in the position of a nominative (marfūʿ) as a fronted khabar (predicate); ﴿ذلك﴾: ﴿ذا﴾ is a demonstrative in the position of a genitive (majrūr) as a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), the lām is for distance, and the kāf is a particle of address.
﴿العذاب﴾: a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿ولعذاب﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya) or resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya); the lām is the lām of inception (lām al-ibtidāʾ); and «عذاب» is a mubtadaʾ.
﴿الآخرة﴾: a muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿أكبر﴾: the khabar. The clause ﴿ولعذاب...﴾ is circumstantial, in the position of an accusative (manṣūb), or resumptive, with no grammatical position.
﴿لو﴾: conditional.
﴿كانوا﴾: «كان» is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, and the wāw of the plural is its noun.
﴿يعلمون﴾: a verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the khabar of «كان», and the apodosis (jawāb) of «لو» is omitted.

muyesser-irab:34-34.t:
﴿إن﴾: an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh).
﴿للمتقين﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate) of «إن».
﴿عند﴾: the adverb is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from «جنات», or attached to the [notion of] settledness (istiqrār) to which the khabar is attached.
﴿ربهم﴾: a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿جنات﴾: the postponed noun of «إن».
﴿النعيم﴾: a muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:35-35.t:
﴿أفنجعل﴾: the hamza is for the interrogative of disavowal (al-istifhām al-inkārī); the fāʾ is a conjunction, and the clause is conjoined to an implied [clause] that the context requires, i.e.: «أنحيف في الحكم فنجعل المسلمين كالكافرين» (shall We be unjust in judgement and make the Muslims like the disbelievers?); ﴿نجعل﴾ is an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir).
﴿المسلمين﴾: the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿كالمجرمين﴾: the kāf is a noun in the sense of «مثل» (like), indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, in the position of an accusative (manṣūb) as the second mafʿūl bihi, and ﴿المجرمين﴾ is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

muyesser-irab:36-36.t:
﴿ما﴾: an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿لكم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of ﴿ما﴾.
﴿كيف﴾: an interrogative noun in the position of an accusative (manṣūb) as a ḥāl (circumstantial).
﴿تحكمون﴾: an imperfect verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the clause «تحكمون» is a badal (substitute) from the clause ﴿ما لكم﴾.

muyesser-irab:37-37.t:
﴿أم﴾: a conjunction for transitional digression (al-iḍrāb al-intiqālī), and the hamza implied in it is for the interrogative of disavowal and rebuke (al-istifhām al-inkārī al-tawbīkhī).
﴿لكم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate).
﴿كتاب﴾: a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿فيه﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿تدرسون﴾.
﴿تدرسون﴾: an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the clause ﴿تدرسون...﴾ is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), or resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:38-38.t:
﴿إن﴾: an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh).
﴿لكم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted fronted khabar (predicate) of «إن».
﴿فيه﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, a ḥāl (circumstantial).
﴿لما﴾: the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), brought for emphasis; and «ما» is the postponed noun of «إن».
﴿تخيرون﴾: an imperfect verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the clause ﴿تخيرون﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:39-39.t:
﴿أم﴾: a conjunction for transitional digression (al-iḍrāb al-intiqālī), and the hamza implied in it is for the interrogative of disavowal and rebuke (al-istifhām al-inkārī al-tawbīkhī).
﴿لكم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate).
﴿أيمان﴾: a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿علينا﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted adjective (ṣifa) of ﴿أيمان﴾.
﴿بالغة﴾: a second adjective.
﴿إلى يوم القيامة﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the [notion of] settledness (istiqrār) to which the khabar, namely «لكم», is attached; or to «بالغة», i.e.: reaching to that day and ending at it; ﴿القيامة﴾ is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿إن﴾: the clause is the answer to the oath that is understood (malḥūẓ), so it has no grammatical position; «إن» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh).
﴿لكم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted fronted khabar of «إن».
﴿لما﴾: the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), brought for emphasis; and «ما» is the postponed noun of «إن».
﴿تحكمون﴾: an imperfect verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the clause ﴿تحكمون﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:40-40.t:
﴿سلهم﴾: the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; «سَلْ» is an imperative verb with its latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent), and ﴿هم﴾ is its first object.
﴿أيّهم﴾: a mubtadaʾ (subject), the pronoun being in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by annexation.
﴿بذلك﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿زعيم﴾.
﴿زعيم﴾: the khabar (predicate) of «أيّهم»; the clause is in the position of an accusative (manṣūb) as the second object of «سَلْ», because it takes two objects in the accusative.

muyesser-irab:41-41.t:
﴿أم﴾: a conjunction for transitional digression (al-iḍrāb al-intiqālī), and the hamza implied in it is for the interrogative of disavowal and rebuke (al-istifhām al-inkārī al-tawbīkhī).
﴿لهم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate).
﴿شركاء﴾: a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); this clause is conjoined in meaning to the clause «أيّهم بذلك زعيم».
﴿فليأتوا﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition); the lām is the lām of command; «يأتوا» is an imperfect verb made jussive (majzūm) by the lām, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent).
﴿بشركائهم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يأتوا﴾.
﴿إن﴾: conditional.
﴿كانوا﴾: a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb in the position of a jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the wāw is its noun.
﴿صادقين﴾: the khabar of «كان»; the apodosis (jawāb) is omitted, indicated by what precedes, i.e.: «فليأتوا بشركائهم» (then let them bring their partners).

muyesser-irab:42-42.t:
﴿يوم﴾: an adverb, the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an implied (muqaddar) «أذكر» (remember), or it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) His saying: ﴿فليأتوا﴾.
﴿يكشف﴾: a clause in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by the annexation of the adverb to it; «يكشف» is an imperfect verb built for the one whose agent is not named (passive).
﴿عن ساق﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
﴿ويدعون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; «يدعون» is an imperfect verb built for the one whose agent is not named (passive), nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil.
﴿إلى السجود﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يدعون﴾.
﴿فلا﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and «لا» is negating.
﴿يستطيعون﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent).

muyesser-irab:43-43.t:
﴿خاشعة﴾: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun of «يدعون».
﴿أبصارهم﴾: the fāʿil (agent) of «خاشعة», the pronoun being in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by annexation.
﴿ترهقهم﴾: a second ḥāl; «ترهقهم» is an imperfect verb, and the pronoun is a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿ذلّة﴾: a postponed fāʿil.
﴿وقد﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and «قد» is a particle of verification (taḥqīq).
﴿كانوا﴾: a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, and the wāw is its noun.
﴿يدعون﴾: a verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil «[Translator's note: so in the source; here «يدعون» is passive and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil, as in the previous verse.]»; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of «كانوا».
﴿إلى السجود﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يدعون﴾.
﴿وهم﴾: the wāw is circumstantial, and «هم» is a mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿سالمون﴾: the khabar, made nominative (marfūʿ) by the wāw.

muyesser-irab:44-44.t:
﴿فذرني﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, or [the fāʾ] al-faṣīḥa, because it is the answer to an implied condition, the implied form being: «إذا كانت أحوالهم كذلك فذرني» (if their states are like that, then leave Me [with them]); «ذر» is an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), and the yāʾ is in the position of an accusative (manṣūb) as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿ومن﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «من» is conjoined to the yāʾ; or the wāw is for accompaniment (maʿiyya), and «من» is in the position of an accusative as a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment); the first is preferable.
﴿يكذب﴾: an imperfect verb, the fāʿil being latent; the clause ﴿يكذب﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.
﴿بهذا﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يكذب﴾.
﴿الحديث﴾: a badal (substitute) from the demonstrative.
﴿سنستدرجهم﴾: a resumptive statement with no grammatical position; the sīn is for the future; «نستدرجهم» is an imperfect verb with a latent fāʿil, and the pronoun is a mafʿūl bihi.
﴿من﴾: an indeclinable (mabnī) preposition with no grammatical position.
﴿حيث﴾: an adverb, indeclinable on ḍamma, in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by «من»; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿نستدرجهم﴾.
﴿لا﴾: negating.
﴿يعلمون﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn; the clause «لا يعلمون» is in the position of a genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it.

muyesser-irab:45-45.t:
﴿وأملي﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; «أملي» is an imperfect verb, and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir).
﴿لهم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أملي﴾.
﴿إن﴾: an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh).
﴿كيدي﴾: the noun of «إن», made accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa, its appearance being prevented by the place being occupied by the vowel suited to the first-person yāʾ; the first-person yāʾ is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿متين﴾: the khabar (predicate) of «إن», made nominative (marfūʿ) by the overt ḍamma; the clause serves as the reason (taʿlīl) for the granting of respite.

muyesser-irab:46-46.t:
﴿أم﴾: conjoined to what precedes; ﴿أم﴾ is a conjunction for transitional digression (al-iḍrāb al-intiqālī).
﴿تسألهم﴾: an imperfect verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent) and a first mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿أجرًا﴾: a second mafʿūl bihi.
﴿فهم﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and «هم» is a mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿من مغرم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿مثقلون﴾.
﴿مثقلون﴾: the khabar (predicate), made nominative (marfūʿ) by the wāw.

muyesser-irab:47-47.t:
﴿أم﴾: conjoined to what precedes; ﴿أم﴾ is a conjunction for transitional digression (al-iḍrāb al-intiqālī).
﴿عندهم﴾: an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate), and the pronoun is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿الغيب﴾: a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿فهم﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and «هم» is a mubtadaʾ.
﴿يكتبون﴾: a verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the khabar.

muyesser-irab:48-48.t:
﴿فاصبر﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition); «اصبر» is an imperative verb, and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being «أنت» (you).
﴿لحكم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿اصبر﴾.
﴿ربك﴾: a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿ولا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «لا» is prohibitive.
﴿تكن﴾: an imperfect verb made jussive (majzūm) by «لا»; its noun is latent, its implied form being «أنت».
﴿كصاحب﴾: the kāf is a noun in the sense of «مثل» (like), indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, in the position of an accusative (manṣūb) as the khabar (predicate) of «تكن», and «صاحب» is a muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿الحوت﴾: a muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿إذ﴾: an adverb attached to an omitted muḍāf, the implied form being: «ولا يكن حالك مثل حال صاحب الحوت وقت ندائه» (and let not your state be like the state of the companion of the fish at the time of his calling out).
﴿نادى﴾: a past verb, the fāʿil being latent; the clause is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by the annexation of the adverb to it.
﴿وهو﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and «هو» is a mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿مكظوم﴾: the khabar; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun of «نادى».

muyesser-irab:49-49.t:
﴿لولا﴾: a particle of non-occurrence due to occurrence (ḥarf imtināʿ li-wujūd), containing the meaning of condition.
﴿أن﴾: a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle.
﴿تداركه﴾: a past verb, and the hāʾ is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿نعمة﴾: the fāʿil (agent); the verb is put in the masculine because the femininity of «النعمة» is not real.
﴿من ربه﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted naʿt (adjective) of ﴿نعمة﴾; «أن» together with what falls within its scope is in the place of a nominative (marfūʿ) as a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is necessarily omitted.
﴿لنبذ﴾: the lām occurs in the apodosis of «لولا»; «نبذ» is a past verb built for the one whose agent is not named (passive), and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being «هو» (he).
﴿بالعراء﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿نبذ﴾.
﴿وهو﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and «هو» is a mubtadaʾ.
﴿مذموم﴾: the khabar; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun of «نبذ».

muyesser-irab:50-50.t:
﴿فاجتباه﴾: the fāʾ conjoins to an implied [clause], i.e.: «فأدركته نعمة من ربه فاجتباه» (then a favour from his Lord reached him, so He chose him); «اجتباه» is a past verb, and the pronoun is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿ربه﴾: the fāʿil (agent), in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the hāʾ is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿فجعله﴾: conjoined to ﴿فاجتباه﴾; the hāʾ is the first mafʿūl bihi.
﴿من الصالحين﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted second object of «جعل».

muyesser-irab:51-51.t:
﴿وإن﴾: the wāw is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya), and the clause after it is resumptive, with no grammatical position; «إن» is lightened from the heavy [«إنّ»] and is inoperative (muhmala).
﴿يكاد﴾: a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, one of the verbs of approximation (afʿāl al-muqāraba).
﴿الذين﴾: a relative noun in the position of a nominative (marfūʿ) as the noun of «يكاد».
﴿كفروا﴾: a past verb, and the wāw of the plural is the fāʿil (agent); the clause ﴿كفروا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.
﴿ليزلقونك﴾: the distinguishing lām (al-lām al-fāriqa); «يزلقونك» is an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil, and the kāf is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿يزلقونك﴾ is in the position of an accusative (manṣūb) as the khabar (predicate) of «يكاد».
﴿بأبصارهم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يزلقونك﴾.
﴿لما﴾: linking, or a temporal adverb (ḥīniyya ẓarfiyya).
﴿سمعوا﴾: a past verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil.
﴿الذكر﴾: a mafʿūl bihi; the apodosis (jawāb) of «لما» is omitted because [the context] indicates it, i.e.: «لما سمعوا الذكر كادوا يزلقونك» (when they heard the Reminder, they almost made you slip).
﴿ويقولون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «يقولون» is conjoined to «يزلقونك».
﴿إنه﴾: «إن» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and the hāʾ is its noun.
﴿لمجنون﴾: the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and «مجنون» is the khabar of «إن»; the clause is the object of their saying.

muyesser-irab:52-52.t:
﴿وما﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and «ما» is negating and inoperative (muhmala), because its negation is broken by «إلا» «[Translator's note: the source has «لانتقاء» (absence), evidently a slip for «لانتقاض» (breaking).]».
﴿هو﴾: a mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿إلا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr).
﴿ذكر﴾: the khabar (predicate) of «هو».
﴿للعالمين﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted naʿt (adjective) of ﴿ذكر﴾.

nahhas-irab:1-2.t:
ن: on this word there are some thirty-odd answers: among them six meanings and six readings, one of which has six answers. Al-Ḥakam ibn Ẓuhayr reported from his father, from Abū Hurayra, who said:
The earths are upon Nūn, Nūn is upon the water, the water is upon the rock, and the rock has four corners, on each corner of which an angel stands in the water. Yazīd reported from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "Alif-Lām-Rā", "Ḥā-Mīm" and "Nūn" are the letters of "al-Raḥmān" separated. In the ḥadīth of Muʿāwiya ibn Qurra, from his father, traced back to the Prophet (marfūʿ), he said: Nūn is a tablet of light. Qatāda said: Nūn is the inkwell. Abū Jaʿfar said: these are four views. It has also been said: the implied form is "and by the Lord of Nūn"; and it has been said: it is a call to attention (tanbīh), as was mentioned earlier regarding «ألم». As for the readings, they are six, as we mentioned. Most people read ن وَالْقَلَمِ with the nūn pronounced distinctly; it has been read with it concealed (ikhfāʾ); it has been read with it assimilated, with nasalization (ghunna) and without nasalization; it is reported from ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar that he read «ن والقلم» [i.e. "nūna", in the accusative] [Translator's note: the unvowelled text does not show the vowel]; and Ibn Isḥāq read «نون والقلم» in the genitive [i.e. "nūni"]. These are six readings. On the accusative one among them there are six answers. Among them: that it is accusative by the action of a verb falling on it, i.e. "mention Nūn".
And it is not declined (lam tanṣarif) because it is the name of the sūra. A second answer: that it is not declined because it is a foreign noun. These two answers are from al-Akhfash Saʿīd. The view of Sībawayh is that it was likened to "ayna" and "kayfa"; the view of al-Farrāʾ is that it was likened to "thumma"; it has been said: it was likened to the nūn of the plural. Abū Ḥātim said: the wāw of the oath was dropped from it, so it became accusative by an implied verb, just as you say "Allāha laqad kāna kadhā" (by Allah, such-and-such happened). Abū Jaʿfar said:
These are eighteen answers. On its being made quiescent there are two views. The position of Sībawayh is that the letters of the alphabet were made quiescent only because they are parts of the letters of nouns, so it was not permissible to inflect them, just as the middle of a noun is not inflected. Some of the Kufans rejected this view, saying: when you say "zāy", you have added an alif and a yāʾ to the letter. He said: sounder than this is the view of al-Farrāʾ, who said: the letters of the alphabet were not inflected because you intended only to teach spelling. Abū Jaʿfar said: this is a sound view, because when you intend to teach spelling it is not permissible to add inflection, for that would remove it from the sense of spelling — unless you qualify it with a naʿt (adjective) or conjoin to it, and then you inflect it. Whoever pronounces the nūn distinctly says: the rule for the letters of spelling is that one pauses on them; moreover, the nūn is far in its point of articulation from the wāw, so it resembled the guttural letters. For this reason no one read with the nūn pronounced distinctly in «كهيعص», because of the closeness of the ṣād to the nūn; al-Kisāʾī assimilated it because he built the speech on continuous reading (waṣl). Whoever assimilates with nasalization wanted not to remove the trace of the nūn; whoever drops the nasalization says: the assimilated letter has taken on the ruling of what it is assimilated into. Whoever reads «نون والقلم» gave it kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. Abū Ḥātim said: he implied the wāw of the oath. If you put "nūn" in the plural, you say:
"nūnāt", taking it as a letter of spelling; if you put it in the plural as a name for the fish, you say for the plural of multitude:
"nīnān", and for the plural of paucity "anwān"; "nūna" is also permissible, like "kūz" and "kūza". وَالْقَلَمِ: genitive by the wāw of the oath. It is the pen that one writes with, except that authoritative instruction (tawqīf) has come that it is the pen with which everything that will be until the Day of Resurrection was written on the Preserved Tablet. Al-Qāsim ibn Abī Bazza reported that from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās; and Muʿāwiya ibn Qurra from his father, tracing it back to the Prophet. وَما يَسْطُرُونَ: a wāw of conjunction, not a wāw of oath; "mā" and the verb form a maṣdar (verbal noun), and it may be in the sense of "alladhī" (that which). The answer to the oath is ما أَنْتَ بِنِعْمَةِ رَبِّكَ بِمَجْنُونٍ: that is, you are not, by what Allah has favoured you with of intellect and understanding — since he was the most intelligent of the people of his time — بِمَجْنُونٍ, which means one whose intellect is covered. From this comes "janna ʿalayhi al-laylu" and "ajannahu" (the night covered him); and from it is said "janīn" (foetus), "janan" for the grave and "mijann" for the shield. ʿUmar ibn Abī Rabīʿa said: [al-Ṭawīl] 496-
وكان مجنّي دون من كنت أتّقي ... ثلاث شخوص كاعبان ومعصر
(My shield against those I was wary of was three figures: two full-breasted girls and one just come of age.)
And it has been said: "jinn", because they are hidden from people's eyes. Heard from the Arabs, against analogy:
"ajanna, fa-huwa majnūn"; the analogical form is "mujann". Abū Jaʿfar said: ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān related to us from Muḥammad ibn Yazīd that he held to analogy in this, as though "majnūn" were said from "junna".

nahhas-irab:3-3.t:
وَإِنَّ لَكَ لَأَجْراً: that is, for delivering the message. غَيْرَ مَمْنُونٍ: it has been said: it is not held over you as a favour; and it has been said:
not cut off.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa reported from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: [you are] upon a religion. Abū Jaʿfar said: so this would be like his saying ﷺ: "The most perfect of the believers in faith is the best of them in character (khuluq)", i.e. the best of them in religion, way, school and obedience. ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her, was asked what the great character was that he had; she said: the Qur'an. It has also been said: it is the cheerfulness he had, his striving to meet people's needs, his honouring them and his gentleness with them.

nahhas-irab:5-6.t:
فَسَتُبْصِرُ وَيُبْصِرُونَ: that is, on the Day of Resurrection. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: I asked Abū ʿUthmān al-Māzinī about this, and he said: this is the end [of the sentence]. Al-Akhfash said: the meaning is "you will see and they will see in which of you is the trial (al-fitna)".
Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: the implied form is "in which of you is the trial of the one tried". Al-Farrāʾ said: the bāʾ is in the sense of «في» (in).
Abū Jaʿfar said: these are the views of the grammarians gathered together. We now mention the views of the exegetes. Sufyān reported from Khuṣayf, from Mujāhid: بِأَيِّكُمُ الْمَفْتُونُ: he said: which of you is the mad one. Al-Ḥasan and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: in which of you is the madness. The view of Qatāda: which of you is closer to Satan. These are three views of the exegetes.
