On the view of Mujāhid, the bāʾ is in the sense of «في», as one says "so-and-so is bi-Makka" and "fī Makka" (in Mecca); and the meaning on that is: you will know and they will know in which of the two parties is the mad one who does not follow the truth — in your party or in theirs. On the view of al-Ḥasan and al-Ḍaḥḥāk: you will know and they will know in which of you is the trial.
And "al-maftūn" in the sense of "al-fitna" and "al-futūn" [i.e. a maṣdar on the pattern mafʿūl], just as one says "he has no intelligence (maʿqūl) and no firm judgement (maʿqūd raʾy)". Abū Jaʿfar said: this is among the best things said about it. The view of Qatāda is that the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida).

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: That is, He knows best who has strayed from His way among the disbelievers of Quraysh. وَهُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِالْمُهْتَدِينَ: [those guided] by you and those who follow you.

nahhas-irab:8-9.t: Conjoined (maʿṭūf), and not an answer; had it been an answer, the nūn would have been dropped from it. Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa reported from Ibn ʿAbbās: وَدُّوا لَوْ تُدْهِنُ فَيُدْهِنُونَ: he said: He says: if you would make concessions to them, they would make concessions. The meaning on this is: they wish you would be soft with them and not condemn their disbelief and sins, so that they would be soft with you, act hypocritically towards you and become bold in sins; and softness in a matter like this is the ruin of religion. It is taken from "duhn" (oil); softening was likened to it.

nahhas-irab:10-10.t: That is, everyone known for swearing falsely; when he is like that, he is contemptible before Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and before the believers. Mujāhid said: مَهِينٍ means weak. Abū Jaʿfar said: on this view "mahīn" is of the pattern faʿīl in its regular sense; and it may be in the sense of "muhān" (despised).

nahhas-irab:11-11.t: هَمَّازٍ: from "hamazahu", when he found fault with him; the root sense of "al-hamz" is "al-ghamz" (pressing, poking). مَشَّاءٍ بِنَمِيمٍ: «مشّاء» is lengthened (mamdūd), because it is an alif followed by a hamza; the alif is faint, and the hamza, because of its remote point of articulation, is hidden, so it was strengthened by the prolongation (madda). Likewise the wāw when what precedes it has ḍamma, as in "al-sūʾā", and likewise the yāʾ when what precedes it has kasra, as in "sīʾa bihim". This is in the connected case (within one word). [As for the separated case,] the grammarians have three views about it. Some of them said: there is no prolongation in it when it is separated. Some said: it is prolonged in the same way as the connected; Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] used to hold this. Some said: prolongation in the separated is more fitting than in the connected, so as to show by the prolongation the separation of one word from the other, as in His saying, Mighty and Majestic: بِما أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكَ [al-Baqara: 4], and likewise فَلَمَّا أَنْ جاءَ الْبَشِيرُ [Yūsuf: 96], and with the wāw and the yāʾ: قُوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ [al-Taḥrīm: 6] and وَفِي أَنْفُسِكُمْ [al-Dhāriyāt: 21]. Reciters are among the people most in need of knowing this. Mistakes sometimes occur in it, and that is a solecism (laḥn). Whoever reads دائِرَةُ السَّوْءِ [al-Tawba: 98] may not prolong this, because what precedes the wāw has fatḥa; whoever reads «دائرة السّوء» [i.e. "al-sūʾi"] prolongs, because what precedes the wāw has ḍamma. This is required for the wāw only when what precedes it has ḍamma, and for the yāʾ when what precedes it has kasra, because they then resemble the alif and become letters of prolongation and softness (madd wa-līn) like the alif, so prolongation is required in them as it was in the alif. And since what precedes the wāw has ḍamma and what precedes the yāʾ has kasra, so that the vowel before each is of its own kind, they became weak and were strengthened by the prolongation. Whoever reads وَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ آمَنُوا [al-Baqara: 103] may not prolong this, because what precedes the wāw has fatḥa. It is said that most of those who err in this are reciters who recite according to the reading of Ḥamza. Abū Jaʿfar said: whoever says "namīm" says "qad namma" [Translator's note: so in the text], "thalāthatu animmatin"; and whoever says "namīma" says "namāʾim".

nahhas-irab:12-12.t: مَنَّاعٍ: a naʿt (adjective), and likewise مُعْتَدٍ; had they both been accusative, that would have been permissible as a naʿt of "kull" [Translator's note: i.e. of "kulla" in the preceding verse وَلا تُطِعْ كُلَّ حَلَّافٍ]; i.e. transgressing against people in his dealings. أَثِيمٍ: opposing his Lord in His command and prohibition, as Qatāda said: sinful towards his Lord.

nahhas-irab:13-13.t:
عُتُلٍّ: the exegetes, among them Abū Razīn and al-Shaʿbī, said: "al-ʿutull" is the harsh one. Al-Farrāʾ said:
that is, fierce in disputing falsely. Someone else said: he is the coarse one, severe in disbelief; its plural is "ʿatāll". بَعْدَ ذلِكَ: it has been said: that is, in addition to that. زَنِيمٍ: also a naʿt (adjective).

nahhas-irab:14-14.t: أَنْ is in the position of the accusative, i.e. "because he was". Al-Ḥasan, Abū Jaʿfar and Ḥamza read «أأن كان ذا مال وبنين». Abū Jaʿfar [al-Naḥḥās] said: this is by way of rebuke, i.e. "is it because he had wealth and sons that he disbelieves, or that you obey him?" [Translator's note: the text reads «أي الآن كان», "i.e. now that he had…"; this is translated according to the evident intended sense «ألأن كان».]

nahhas-irab:16-16.t: Abū Jaʿfar said: we have mentioned several views about it. Among them is what Maʿmar reported from Qatāda, who said: on his nose. Among what is mentioned is that Saʿīd reported from Qatāda: سَنَسِمُهُ عَلَى الْخُرْطُومِ (16): he said: a disgrace that will not leave him. This is among the best things said about it, i.e. We will expose his affair and make it notorious until it becomes evident, and he will be like one branded on his nose. That said, it is reported from Ibn ʿAbbās on سَنَسِمُهُ عَلَى الْخُرْطُومِ: he said: he fought on the day of Badr, was struck a blow with a sword, and it became a brand on him.

nahhas-irab:17-17.t: إِنَّا بَلَوْناهُمْ: that is, We charged them with the duty of gratitude for favours and of giving the poor their rights, which We made obligatory in their wealth. كَما بَلَوْنا أَصْحابَ الْجَنَّةِ: Ibn ʿAbbās said: they were people of the Book. إِذْ أَقْسَمُوا لَيَصْرِمُنَّها: that is, they would surely cut [its fruit]. "Al-jidhādh" is cutting; from it [comes] "ṣarama fulānun fīnā" (so-and-so cut off ties among us) and "sayfun ṣārim" (a sharp sword). مُصْبِحِينَ: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). "Aṣbaḥa" means "entered upon the morning".

nahhas-irab:18-18.t: And they do not say "if Allah wills", and they were blamed for this, because when a person says "I shall certainly do such-and-such", he cannot be sure that he will not be cut off from it and so be a liar; so he must say "if Allah wills".

nahhas-irab:19-19.t: It has been said: a fire was sent upon it and burned their crops. وَهُمْ نائِمُونَ: in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:20-20.t: That is, like something cropped, cut off. "Ṣarīm" in the sense of "maṣrūm", like "qatīl" in the sense of "maqtūl".

nahhas-irab:22-22.t: أَنِ is in the position of the accusative, i.e. "bi-an" (that); it may also have no position, being explicative (tafsīr). إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صارِمِينَ: "kuntum" is in the position of the jussive by the condition; it does without the apodosis (jawāb) because of what preceded, since it is a past verb.

nahhas-irab:23-23.t: In the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:24-24.t: The answer concerning أَنْ is as given before. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] it is without «أن», because the meaning of يَتَخافَتُونَ is "they say secretly".

nahhas-irab:25-25.t: The soundest thing said about its meaning is "with set purpose", as Mujāhid said: they had laid that down among themselves, i.e. they did it with purpose, groundwork and conspiracy among themselves, thinking themselves able to do it.

nahhas-irab:26-26.t: That is, we have lost the way, and this is not our garden — when they saw it burned.

nahhas-irab:27-27.t: It has been said: then one who recognized it and knew that they had not lost the way said: بَلْ نَحْنُ مَحْرُومُونَ (27): that is, we have been deprived of its fruits because of what we did.

nahhas-irab:28-28.t: Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa reported from Ibn ʿAbbās: قالَ أَوْسَطُهُمْ: that is, the most just of them. أَلَمْ أَقُلْ لَكُمْ لَوْلا تُسَبِّحُونَ: that is, "why do you not" (hallā).

nahhas-irab:29-29.t: قالُوا سُبْحانَ رَبِّنا إِنَّا كُنَّا ظالِمِينَ (29). قالُوا سُبْحانَ رَبِّنا: accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun). إِنَّا كُنَّا ظالِمِينَ: that is, we put the thing in other than its place by withholding what was due from us; and likewise "ẓulm" (wrongdoing) in the language is putting a thing in other than its place.

nahhas-irab:30-30.t: In the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:31-31.t: قالُوا يا وَيْلَنا: a vocative of a muḍāf; the point of it is that its meaning is "this is the time for woe to be present". إِنَّا كُنَّا طاغِينَ: that is, in our opposing the command of our Lord and going beyond it.

nahhas-irab:32-32.t: Sībawayh reported that some of the Arabs drop «أن» with "ʿasā", likening it to "laʿalla". إِلى رَبِّنا راغِبُونَ: that is, [desirous] that He give us in exchange something better than it.

nahhas-irab:33-33.t: كَذلِكَ الْعَذابُ: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate), and likewise وَلَعَذابُ الْآخِرَةِ أَكْبَرُ. It is called "ākhira" because it is last (ākhira) after a first; and it has been said: because it comes later for people. لَوْ كانُوا يَعْلَمُونَ: «لو» is followed only by a verb, because it resembles the conditional particles.

nahhas-irab:34-34.t: جَنَّاتِ: accusative by "inna", and the sign of the accusative is the kasra of the tāʾ; however, al-Akhfash used to say: it is indeclinable (mabnī), not inflected, in the position of the accusative.

nahhas-irab:35-35.t: كَالْمُجْرِمِينَ: the kāf is in the position of the accusative, a second object.

nahhas-irab:36-36.t: "Mā" is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); it is a complete noun, and لَكُمْ is the khabar (predicate). كَيْفَ is in the position of the accusative by "taḥkumūna".

nahhas-irab:37-37.t: أَمْ لَكُمْ كِتابٌ فِيهِ تَدْرُسُونَ (37): that is, do you have a book that has come to you from Allah, in which you study?

nahhas-irab:38-39.t: إِنَّ لَكُمْ فِيهِ لَما تَخَيَّرُونَ (38): that is, for yourselves, against Us. «إن» was given kasra because the lām comes after it. Likewise أَمْ لَكُمْ أَيْمانٌ عَلَيْنا بالِغَةٌ إِلى يَوْمِ الْقِيامَةِ: that is, or do you have oaths that We swore to you, extending to the Day of Resurrection, that yours is what you judge? In the reading of al-Ḥasan, «بالغة» ] is in the accusative ("bālighatan"). Al-Farrāʾ said: as a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "truly". Someone else said: as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent pronoun in "ʿalaynā".

nahhas-irab:41-41.t: That is, partners who help them and bear witness for them.

nahhas-irab:42-42.t:
يَوْمَ يُكْشَفُ عَنْ ساقٍ: this is the reading held by the body [of reciters] that constitutes the proof; what is reported other than it is subject to inconsistency, as are most readings that depart from the body [of reciters], even if they occur in sound chains of transmission, since they come by way of single reports (āḥād). Among these is what was read before Ibrāhīm ibn Mūsā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Jahm, who said: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us: Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he read «يوم تكشف عن ساق» ("the day it uncovers a shank"), meaning the Resurrection and the Hour, because of its severity. Abū Jaʿfar said:
This is a sound chain, yet what we have mentioned occurred in it: as was read before Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥajjāj, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Makhzūmī and a group of Sufyān's companions, who said: Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAmr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he read «يوم نكشف عن ساق» with the nūn ("the day We uncover"). Sufyān al-Thawrī reported from Salama [ibn] Kuhayl, from Abū Ṣādiq, from Ibn Masʿūd, that he read «يوم نكشف عن ساق» with the nūn. Sufyān al-Thawrī also reported from Salama, from Abū al-Zaʿrāʾ, from Ibn Masʿūd, that he read «يوم يكشف عن ساق» with fatḥa on the yāʾ and kasra on the shīn ("yakshifu"). What the exegetes hold is that the meaning is "the day severity is uncovered"; that is well known in the speech of the Arabs. The meaning may also be "the day people uncover their shanks because of the severity of what they are in"; that is used in the speech of the Arabs. "Sāq" is feminine and takes the hāʾ in the diminutive.
وَيُدْعَوْنَ إِلَى السُّجُودِ فَلا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ: it has been said: they are called to prostrate only to be rebuked by it, and it is said to them:
"You were called to the prostration that would benefit you in the world, and you refused; so come, prostrate now" — because it is not an abode of testing and prostration does not benefit there. The meaning on this is: they are unable to prostrate with a prostration from which they would benefit. And it has been said: rather, their backs dry up [stiffen] as a punishment, so they are unable to prostrate.

nahhas-irab:43-43.t: خاشِعَةً: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). أَبْصارُهُمْ: nominative by "khushūʿ" [i.e. as agent of "khāshiʿa"]; it is also permissible to put both in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate). تَرْهَقُهُمْ ذِلَّةٌ: also in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl; it may also be cut off from the first. وَقَدْ كانُوا يُدْعَوْنَ إِلَى السُّجُودِ وَهُمْ سالِمُونَ: that is, in the world.

nahhas-irab:44-44.t:
مَنْ is in the position of the accusative, conjoined; or, if you wish, it is a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment). الْحَدِيثِ سَنَسْتَدْرِجُهُمْ مِنْ حَيْثُ لا يَعْلَمُونَ: there are two views on its meaning. One of them: We will give them enjoyment and amplitude in this world until they imagine that they have good, and are deluded by the blessing and joy they are in; then We seize them suddenly, as Abū Mūsā reported from the Prophet ﷺ: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, gives the wrongdoer respite, until when He seizes him He does not let him escape." Then he recited:
وَكَذلِكَ أَخْذُ رَبِّكَ إِذا أَخَذَ الْقُرى وَهِيَ ظالِمَةٌ. And it has been said: We will draw them step by step from their graves to the Fire.

nahhas-irab:45-45.t: وَأُمْلِي لَهُمْ: with the yāʾ quiescent; the original is ḍamma on it, because it is an imperfect verb, and the ḍamma was dropped because of its heaviness. إِنَّ كَيْدِي مَتِينٌ: that is, strong and severe.

nahhas-irab:46-46.t: The reading of Nāfiʿ is with ḍamma on the first mīm and the second quiescent. Abū Jaʿfar said: he brought the first according to the original form, and chose this because when it meets a connecting alif (alif waṣl) it takes ḍamma and nothing else, so he treated the disjunctive alif (alif qaṭʿ) in the same way. It has also been said: he brought both forms together, as he read مِنْ بَعْدِ ما قَنَطُوا [al-Shūrā: 28] and read لا تَقْنَطُوا [al-Zumar: 53]. Few of his companions or others argue for him [on this]. [Translator's note: the verse referred to is not quoted in the entry; it is أَمْ تَسْأَلُهُمْ أَجْراً فَهُمْ مِنْ مَغْرَمٍ مُثْقَلُونَ; the words discussed are not named.]

nahhas-irab:47-47.t: أَمْ عِنْدَهُمُ الْغَيْبُ فَهُمْ يَكْتُبُونَ (47): Abū Jaʿfar said: this verse is among the most difficult in the sūra. The upshot of its meaning, according to what has been said — and Allah knows best — is: or do they have the Preserved Tablet, in which all hidden things are, so that they write from it what they dispute with you about, and claim that, despite their disbelief in Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and their rejecting you after the proofs, they are better than you and are upon the truth?

nahhas-irab:48-48.t:
فَاصْبِرْ لِحُكْمِ رَبِّكَ: that is, be patient in delivering the message, bear their harm, and do not hasten the punishment for them. وَلا تَكُنْ كَصاحِبِ الْحُوتِ: in what he did, leaving his people and being distressed at the delay of the punishment from them. إِذْ نادى وَهُوَ مَكْظُومٌ: Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa reported from Ibn ʿAbbās: وَهُوَ مَكْظُومٌ: he said:
grieved. Abū Jaʿfar said: "al-makẓūm" in the speech of the Arabs is one who is grieved and finds no one to whom he can unburden himself; he has suppressed (kaẓama) his anger, i.e. concealed it.

nahhas-irab:49-49.t: لَوْلا أَنْ تَدارَكَهُ نِعْمَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّهِ: in the reading of Ibn Masʿūd, «لولا أن تداركته», making "niʿma" feminine; and the masculine is used because it is a non-real feminine. It is reported from al-Aʿraj: «لولا أن تدّاركه» with doubled dāl, the origin being "tatadārakuhu", the tāʾ assimilated into the dāl. لَنُبِذَ بِالْعَراءِ وَهُوَ مَذْمُومٌ: in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:50-50.t: It has been said: the meaning is "and He, Mighty and Majestic, described him as one of the righteous"; Sībawayh reported "jaʿala" in the sense of "waṣafa" (described). And it has been said: فَجَعَلَهُ مِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ: Allah the Exalted granted him success in obeying Him until he became righteous.

nahhas-irab:51-51.t:
The Kufans say: إِنْ is in the sense of «ما» (not), and the lām in the sense of "illā" (except). The Basrans say:
it is the doubled "inna"; when it was lightened, the verb came after it and the lām of emphasis became necessary with it, to distinguish between negation and affirmation. One of the Kufan grammarians mentioned that this is [about] affliction by the evil eye; one of the scholars considered him ignorant and said: they used to say only "we strike with the eye what we admire and marvel at for its excellence"; this is not of that kind; rather they used to look at the Prophet ﷺ with a look of hatred and aversion.
So the meaning on this is that, because of the sharpness of their look at him, they almost remove him from his place. One says "azlaqa al-ḥajjāmu al-shaʿra" and "zallafahu" when he shaves it. And it has been read لَيُزْلِقُونَكَ from "azlaqa" and "zalaqa", i.e. in both forms.

nahhas-irab:52-52.t: A mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); the pronoun refers back to the reminder (al-dhikr) mentioned before.

safi-cedvel:1-4.t:
* I'rab:
(والقلم) attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb, its implied form being "I swear"; (الواو) conjunction; (ما) an infinitival particle [Note: Or a relative noun in the position of genitive, with the referent pronoun omitted, i.e. what they write down, and the agent pronoun refers to the recording angels.].
The interpreted maṣdar (ما يسطرون) is in the position of genitive, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to القلم.
The clause «(أقسم) بالقلم ...» has no grammatical position: initial (ibtidāʾiyya).
The clause «يسطرون ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (ما).
2- (ما) negative, governing as ليس governs; (بنعمة) attached to the sense of negation in (ما), and (الباء) is causal [Note: I.e. your being mad is negated because of the favour of your Lord upon you. It is not valid to attach it to مجنون, lest it convey the negation of a madness that is a favour from Allah, and there is no madness in existence that is a favour.]; (مجنون) genitive in form, accusative in position, as khabar (predicate) of ما ...
The clause «ما أنت ... بمجنون» has no grammatical position: response to the oath. 3- (الواو) conjunction; (لك) attached to the khabar of إنّ; (اللام) for emphasis, in the place of the lām of the oath; (غير) a naʿt (adjective) of (أجرا), accusative.
The clause «إنّ لك لأجرا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the response to the oath.
4- (الواو) the wāw of conjunction; (اللام) for emphasis, in the place of the lām of the oath, in substitution for the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); (على خلق) attached to the khabar of إنّ.
The clause «إنّك لعلى خلق ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the response to the oath.

* Rhetoric:
The device of verbal correspondence (al-munāsaba al-lafẓiyya): in His words «ن وَالْقَلَمِ وَما يَسْطُرُونَ» and what follows, up to His words «غَيْرَ مَمْنُونٍ». This device consists in bringing words that are balanced in measure.
Metaphor in particles: in His words «وَإِنَّكَ لَعَلى خُلُقٍ عَظِيمٍ».
على in its literal sense conveys elevation over something (istiʿlāʾ), which is not intended in the verse, since the Messenger, upon him be peace, does not rise above the tremendous character and mount it, as a man mounts the back of a horse, for example. Rather it is by way of figurative usage and metaphor; by it is meant the Messenger's, upon him be peace, firm possession of the tremendous character and noble traits.

* Benefits:
- Good character:
Jābir related that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Allah sent me to complete noble traits of character and to complete good deeds." From al-Nawwās ibn Samʿān, who said: I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about righteousness and sin, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Righteousness is good character, and sin is what wavers in your chest and you dislike that people should come to know of it." From ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "The believer, by his good character, attains the rank of one who fasts and stands in prayer." Abū Dāwūd narrated it.
From Abū l-Dardāʾ: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "There is nothing heavier in the scale of the believer on the Day of Resurrection than good character, and Allah the Exalted hates the obscene, foul-mouthed person." al-Tirmidhī narrated it
and said:
a ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ hadith.
From Jābir, may Allah be pleased with him: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Among the most beloved of you to Allah and the nearest of you to me in seating on the Day of Resurrection are those of you best in character."
From Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I served the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for ten years, and by Allah he never once said "uff" to me, nor did he say about anything: why did you do such-and-such, or why did you not do such-and-such.
5- 6

safi-cedvel:5-6.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) linking the apodosis of an implied condition; (بأيّكم) attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (المفتون) [Note: With a muḍāf omitted, i.e. the trial of the one tried; or without omission if المفتون is a maṣdar.], and (أيّ) is an interrogative noun.
The clause «ستبصر ...» is in the position of jussive as apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e.: if the command of Allah comes, you will see [Note: The command of Allah is the Day of Resurrection according to one view, or the victory of the believers in this world according to another view.].
The clause «يبصرون ...» is in the position of jussive, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause ستبصر.
The clause «بأيّكم المفتون» is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the verb of seeing, which is suspended (muʿallaq) by أيّ [Note: Visual seeing is suspended — with fatḥa on the lām — from governing, according to the correct view, by the evidence of: أما ترى أيّ برق هاهنا ("Do you not see what lightning is here") ... and تبصر means ترى.].

* Morphology:
(المفتون): passive participle of the triliteral (فتن). Its pattern is مفعول.
It may also be a maṣdar, like المعقول and الميسور.
7-

safi-cedvel:7-7.t:
* I'rab:
(هو) a detached pronoun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), whose khabar (predicate) is (أعلم); (بمن) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أعلم); (عن سبيله) attached to (ضلّ); (الواو) conjunction; (بالمهتدين) attached to the second (أعلم).
The clause «إنّ ربّك ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive, containing the sense of a causal explanation of what precedes it.
The clause «هو أعلم ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar of إنّ.
The clause «ضلّ ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (من).
The clause «هو أعلم» (the second) is in the position of nominative, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause هو أعلم (the first).
8- 16

safi-cedvel:8-16.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) linking the apodosis of an implied condition; (لا) a prohibitive, jussive-governing particle, and the verb was vowelled with kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters.
The clause «لا تطع ...» is in the position of jussive as apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e.: if the deniers have gone astray, then do not obey them.
9- 13 (لو) an infinitival particle; (الفاء) conjunction; (الواو) conjunction; (مهين، همّاز، مشّاء، منّاع، معتد، أثيم، عتّل، زنيم) adjectives qualifying (حلّاف), genitive like it; (بنميم) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (مشّاء); (للخير) attached to (منّاع) [Note: Or the lām is redundant (zāʾida), for strengthening, and (الخير) is genitive in form, accusative in position, as mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of منّاع.]; (بعد) an accusative adverb, attached to (زنيم), and the reference in (ذلك) is to the aforementioned preceding attributes ...
The interpreted maṣdar (لو تدهن ...) is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi of the verb ودّوا ...
The clause «ودّوا ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) — or a causal explanation of the prohibition. The clause «تدهن ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (لو).
The clause «يدهنون ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause تدهن.
The clause «لا تطع» (the second) is in the position of jussive, conjoined to the clause لا تطع (the first).
14- 16 (أن) an infinitival particle; (عليه) attached to (تتلى); (آياتنا) nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (أساطير) khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "هي".
The interpreted maṣdar (أن كان ...) is in the position of genitive by an omitted preposition, namely the lām, i.e. because he is possessed of ..., attached to an omitted verb indicated by the coming condition with its protasis and apodosis, i.e. he denied the signs of Allah because he was ...
The clause «كان ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the particle relative (أن).
The clause «تتلى عليه آياتنا ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position: apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «سنسمه ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption.

* Morphology:
(10) حلّاف: intensive form of the active participle of the triliteral حلف. Its pattern is فعّال, with fatḥa on the fāʾ and a doubled ʿayn with fatḥa.
(11) همّاز: intensive form of the active participle of the triliteral همز, of the class of ضرب: one who finds fault with others and backbites them, or one who strikes people with his hand. Its pattern is فعّال.
(مشّاء): intensive form of the active participle of the triliteral مشى. Its pattern is فعّال.
(نميم): it was said that it is a maṣdar like النميمة, and it was said that it is the plural of النميمة, or a collective noun (ism jamʿ) for it, from the verb نمّ, of the class of نصر or the class of ضرب ... In al-Miṣbāḥ: النميمة is a noun, and النميم also ... Its pattern is فعيل.
(13) عتّل: meaning coarse and harsh, and it was said: fierce in disputing; a ṣifa mushabbaha (assimilated adjective) from the triliteral عتل, of the class of ضرب. Its pattern is فعلّ with two ḍammas and a doubled lām.
(زنيم): meaning one of doubtful descent, or a base person known for his baseness; a ṣifa mushabbaha, its pattern being فعيل in the sense of فاعل, i.e. one attached to the people like the زنمة of a camel or sheep, which is the piece of the ear that is cut and left hanging, to identify it.
(16) نسمه: it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion, for it is the imperfect of the mithāl weak verb وسم; its fāʾ was deleted in the imperfect, for it is a mithāl weak verb with kasra on the ʿayn in the imperfect. Its pattern is نعله, with fatḥa on the nūn and kasra on the ʿayn.
(الخرطوم): a noun meaning the nose. Its pattern is فعلول with ḍamma then sukūn, like زنبور.

* Rhetoric:
Metonymy (al-kināya): in His words «سَنَسِمُهُ عَلَى الْخُرْطُومِ».
He expressed it so as a metonymy for the utmost humiliation, because a brand on the face is a disfigurement — so much so that he ﷺ forbade it in animals and cursed the one who does it — so how much more so on the most honoured place of it, which is the nose, because of its prominence. It has been said: beauty is in the nose; they made it the seat of honour and pride, and derived from it الأنفة (disdain). And in the word الخرطوم there is contempt, because it is used only of the elephant and the pig; so in expressing the nose by this name there is a reinforcement (tarshīḥ) of the humiliation indicated by branding on that particular organ. What is meant is: We will disgrace him in this world, and humiliate him to the utmost degree.
17- 33

safi-cedvel:17-33.t:
* I'rab:
(ما) an infinitival particle; (إذ) an adverb of past time, in the position of accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (بلونا); (اللام) the lām of the oath; (يصرمنّها) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the retention of the nūn, which was deleted because of the succession of identical letters; the (الواو), deleted because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, is the fāʿil (agent); (النون) is the nūn of emphasis; and (ها) is an object pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), referring to the garden, i.e. its fruit; (مصبحين) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of يصرمنّ.
The interpreted maṣdar (ما بلونا ...) is in the position of genitive by the kāf, attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) whose governor is بلوناهم.
The clause «إنّا بلوناهم ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «بلوناهم ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar (predicate) of إنّ.
The clause «بلونا ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (ما).
The clause «أقسموا ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «يصرمنّها ...» has no grammatical position: response to the oath.
18- (الواو) parenthetical [Note: Or circumstantial (ḥāliyya).]; (لا) negative ...
The clause «لا يستثنون ...» has no grammatical position: parenthetical [Note: Or it is in the position of nominative as khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "هم" ... and the nominal clause is a ḥāl.].
19- (الفاء) conjunction; (عليها) attached to (طاف); (من ربّك) attached to a naʿt (adjective) of طائف; (الواو) circumstantial ...
The clause «طاف عليها طائف ...» is in the position of genitive, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause أقسموا.
The clause «هم نائمون ...» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl.
20- (الفاء) conjunction; (كالصريم) attached to an omitted khabar of أصبحت ...
The clause «أصبحت ...» is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the clause طاف ...
21- 22 (الفاء) conjunction; (مصبحين) is like the first; (أن) an explicative particle (ḥarf tafsīr) [Note: Or an infinitival particle ... and the interpreted maṣdar (أن اغدوا ...) is in the position of genitive by an omitted bāʾ, attached to (تنادوا).]; (على حرثكم) attached to (اغدوا), in the sense of "come forward"; (كنتم) an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb in the position of jussive as protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ).
The clause «تنادوا ...» is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the clause أصبحت.
The clause «اغدوا ...» has no grammatical position: explicative (tafsīriyya).
The clause «كنتم صارمين ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive ... and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes.
23- 24 (الفاء) conjunction; (الواو) circumstantial; (أن) like the first, with both possibilities; (لا) a prohibitive, jussive-governing particle; (يدخلنّها) an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, in the position of jussive; (اليوم) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to (يدخلنّها), and likewise (عليكم) ...
The clause «انطلقوا ...» is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the clause تنادوا.
The clause «هم يتخافتون ...» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl.
The clause «لا يدخلنّها ... مسكين» has no grammatical position: explicative.
25- (الواو) conjunction; (على حرد) attached to (قادرين), which is the khabar of the incomplete verb غدوا [Note: It may be a ḥāl of the third-person pronoun in غدوا if the verb is complete (tāmm), in the sense of "they went out in the early morning".] ...
The clause «غدوا ...» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause هم يتخافتون [Note: Or in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of the fāʿil of يتخافتون, after the circumstantial wāw, with قد implied.]. 26- 27 (رأوها) a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif, which was deleted because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; (اللام) the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), for emphasis; (بل) for digression (iḍrāb) ...
The clause «رأوها ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position: apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «إنّا لضالّون ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «نحن محرومون» has no grammatical position: a resumption within the scope of the saying.
28- (الهمزة) for reproachful interrogation; (لكم) attached to (أقل); (لولا) a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ).
The clause «قال أوسطهم ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «لم أقل ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of speech.
The clause «لولا تسبّحون» has no [grammatical] position: a resumption within the scope of the first saying [Note: The second object of speech is omitted, its implied form being: keep away from disobedience.].
29- (سبحان) a mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb, accusative.
The clause «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «(نسبّح) سبحان ...» has no grammatical position: parenthetical, a supplication.
The clause «إنّا كنّا ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of speech.
The clause «كنّا ظالمين» is in the position of nominative as khabar of إنّ.
30- 32 (الفاء) resumptive; (على بعض) attached to (أقبل); (يا) a particle of the vocative and of lamentation; (ويلنا) one addressed in the vocative (munādā), a muḍāf, lamented over, accusative; (أن) an infinitival and subjunctive-governing particle; (خيرا) a second mafʿūl bihi; (منها) attached to (خيرا); (إلى ربّنا) attached to (راغبون) by its being made to carry (taḍmīn) the meaning of راجعون "returning".
The clause «أقبل بعضهم ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يتلاومون ...» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of بعضهم. The clause «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) [Note: Or in the position of accusative as a ḥāl, with قد implied.].
The clause «النداء والتحسّر» (the vocative and lamentation) has no grammatical position: parenthetical, a supplication.
The clause «إنّا كنّا ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of speech.
The clause «كنّا طاغين» is in the position of nominative as khabar of إنّ.
The clause «عسى ربّنا ...» has no grammatical position: a resumption within the scope of the saying.
The clause «يبدلنا ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the particle relative (أن).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يبدلنا) is in the position of accusative as khabar of عسى.
The clause «إنّا ... راغبون» has no grammatical position: causal (taʿlīliyya).
33- (كذلك) attached to an omitted fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (العذاب); (الواو) conjunction; (اللام) the lām of inception (lām al-ibtidāʾ), for emphasis; (لو) a non-jussive conditional particle ...
The clause «كذلك العذاب ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «عذاب الآخرة أكبر ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «كانوا يعلمون ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive ... and the apodosis is omitted, its implied form being "they would not have opposed Our command".
The clause «يعلمون ...» is in the position of accusative as khabar of كانوا ...

* Morphology:
(18) يستثنون: it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by making quiescent and iʿlāl by deletion. Its original form is يستثنيون — with a yāʾ with ḍamma before the wāw. The ḍamma was felt heavy on the yāʾ, so it was made quiescent and the vowel was transferred to the nūn — iʿlāl by making quiescent; when two quiescent letters met, the yāʾ was deleted — iʿlāl by deletion. Its pattern is يستفعون.
(19) طاف: it contains iʿlāl by substitution; its original form is طوف, its imperfect being يطوف; the wāw was vowelled after a fatḥa, so it was changed into alif.
(نائمون): plural of نائم, active participle of the triliteral نام. Its pattern is فاعل, and the weak letter was changed into hamza by regular substitution.
(20) الصريم: a noun for the night of intense darkness, because of its being cut off (انصرام) from the day; or a noun for the orchard whose fruits have been cut, so it is فعيل in the sense of مفعول ... الصريم may also be applied to a large stretch of sand.
(22) اغدوا: it contains iʿlāl by deletion, beginning from the imperfect ... its original form in the imperfect is يغدوون — with a wāw with ḍamma after the dāl; then the vowel of the wāw was transferred to the dāl before it because of heaviness, and when two quiescent letters met, the wāw, the lām of the word, was deleted ... then the iʿlāl was carried over to the imperative اغدوا. Its pattern is افعوا.
(صارمين): plural of صارم, active participle of the triliteral صرم. Its pattern is فاعل.
(25) غدوا: it contains iʿlāl by deletion; the lām of the word was deleted because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. Its pattern is فعوا.
(حرد): the maṣdar of the triliteral حرد meaning "to intend", of the class of ضرب. Its pattern is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn. It was said that its meaning is prevention, and it was said anger and rancour, and it may be of the class of فرح; and it was said it is withdrawing apart, of the class of نصر.
(32) راغبون: plural of راغب, active participle of the triliteral رغب. Its pattern is فاعل.

* Rhetoric:
Switching to the imperfect: in His words «وَلا يَسْتَثْنُونَ».
I.e. not making exception. In switching to the imperfect there is a kind of expression and a drawing of attention to the place of their error. [Translator's note: the source has «نوع تعبير» "a kind of expression"; «تعيير» "reproach" may be intended. Translated as written.]
Simile (al-tashbīh): in His words «فَأَصْبَحَتْ كَالصَّرِيمِ».
It is likened to the orchard whose fruits have been cut, so that nothing remained in it. It was said: الصريم is the night, i.e. it became burnt, resembling the night in blackness. And it was said: like the morning, in that it became white like harvested crops.
Dependent metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-tabaʿiyya): in His words «أَنِ اغْدُوا عَلى حَرْثِكُمْ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صارِمِينَ».
غدا عليه is said when one raids; so He has likened their going out early to cut the fruit to an army's going out early against something, because the sense of overpowering and seizing is present in it, namely cutting and severing; this is by way of dependent metaphor. The metaphor may also be considered representative (tamthīliyya).

* Benefits:
- The owners of the garden:
From Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The garden was an orchard in Yemen called «al-Ḍarawān», two parasangs short of Ṣanʿāʾ, which the people of the road would tread. It had been planted by people of prayer. It belonged to a man who died, and three sons of his inherited it. He used to leave for the poor — when they cut their palms — everything the sickle passed over, and he used to take from it a year's provision and give the rest in charity to the poor. When the father died and the three sons inherited it, they said: By Allah, the wealth is little and the dependants are many; this was done only when the wealth was much or the dependants few, but now there is no room for us to do as our father used to do. And they plotted among themselves to go early, before people woke, so as not to give the poor anything. [Translator's note: the source prints «قيل» ("it was said"); «قبل» ("before") is evidently intended and is translated.] So they set off whispering among themselves, so that no one would hear them, but they found that orchard had turned black and dry, so they blamed one another and regretted their deed.
34-

safi-cedvel:34-34.t:
* I'rab:
(للمتّقين) attached to (mutaʿalliq) a fronted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (جنّات); (عند) an adverb of place, accusative, attached to the omitted khabar.
The clause «إنّ للمتّقين ... جنّات» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
35-

safi-cedvel:35-35.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for disapproving interrogation (istifhām inkārī) — and for reproach and rebuke; (الفاء) conjunction; (كالمجرمين) attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted second mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
The clause «نجعل ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to an implied resumptive clause, i.e.: are We unjust in judgement, so that We make the Muslims like the criminals?

* Rhetoric:
The inverted simile (al-tashbīh al-maqlūb): in His words «أَفَنَجْعَلُ الْمُسْلِمِينَ كَالْمُجْرِمِينَ».
The basis of the speech is: shall We make the criminals like the Muslims? But it was reversed, going along with their belief that they are better than the Muslims. If, however, the meaning is taken to be that the doers of good are not like the corrupters, nor the God-fearing like the wicked, nor the Muslims like the criminals, in evil state, then there is no reversal in the simile.

safi-cedvel:36-36.t:
* I'rab:
(ما) an interrogative noun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (لكم) attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ ما; (كيف) an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), whose governor is تحكمون ...
The clause «ما لكم ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «تحكمون» has no grammatical position: a badal (substitute) of the clause ما لكم [Note: If the pause is complete at (لكم), the clause is resumptive.].

safi-cedvel:37-38.t:
* I'rab:
(أم) disconnected (munqaṭiʿa), in the sense of بل and the interrogative hamza conveying reproach and rebuke; (لكم) attached to (mutaʿalliq) a fronted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (كتاب); (فيه) attached to (تدرسون); the second (لكم) is the khabar of إنّ; the second (فيه) is attached to the khabar of إنّ; (اللام) for emphasis; (ما) a relative in the position of accusative as the noun of إنّ; (تخيّرون) an imperfect verb from which one of the two tāʾs has been deleted, and from which the third-person referent pronoun has been deleted, i.e. تخيّرونه.
The clause «لكم كتاب ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «تدرسون ...» is in the position of nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of كتاب [Note: The pronoun in (فيه) may refer to their judgement, understood from the previous question, not to the book; it is then attached to the preceding "being settled" (istiqrār) to which (لكم) is attached. On that view the clause تدرسون is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in (فيه) ... or it is resumptive.].
The clause «إنّ لكم فيه لما ...» is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the verb of studying [Note: It is a reported (maḥkiyya) clause, i.e. it is what is studied in the book. The hamza of (إنّ) was due to have fatḥa, but the emphatic lām in its scope made the hamza take kasra.].
The clause «تخيّرون ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (ما).

* Benefits:
- Some of what is hidden in the clause reported by "saying":
Among reported clauses there are some that may be hidden. Of these, in what is reported after "saying": (فَحَقَّ عَلَيْنا قَوْلُ رَبِّنا إِنَّا لَذائِقُونَ). The basis is "you will surely taste My punishment"; then it was switched to the first person, because they spoke of that about themselves, as al-Farazdaq said:
ألم تر أني يوم جوّ سويقة ... بكيت فنادتني هنيدة ماليا
(Did you not see that on the day of Jaww Suwayqa I wept, and Hunayda called to me: "What is the matter with me?")
The basis is: مالك ("what is the matter with you"). And of it, in what is reported after something containing the meaning of saying, is His words: (أَمْ لَكُمْ كِتابٌ فِيهِ تَدْرُسُونَ. إِنَّ لَكُمْ فِيهِ لَما تَخَيَّرُونَ), i.e. you study in it this wording, or you study in it Our saying this speech. That is either on the view that they were addressed with that in the book, according to their claim; or the basis is "they shall surely have what they choose", then it was switched to address when facing them. And it has been said about His words «يَدْعُوا لَمَنْ ضَرُّهُ أَقْرَبُ مِنْ نَفْعِهِ» that يدعو is in the sense of يقول ("says"), like it in the words of ʿAntara:
يدعون عنتر والرماح كأنها ... أشطان بئر في لبان الأدهم
(They call "ʿAntar!" while the spears are like well-ropes in the breast of the black horse.)
— for whoever narrates it «عنتر» with ḍamma, as a vocative — and that (من) in the aforementioned verse is a mubtadaʾ, and (لبئس المولى) its khabar, and what is between them is a nominal clause as ṣila; and the clause of (من) with its khabar is reported by يدعو, i.e. the disbeliever says that on the Day of Resurrection. And it was said: من is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, i.e. "is his god", and that this is a report of what he says in this world; on this view the basis is: he says "the idol is his god"; then the idol was expressed as "one whose harm is nearer than his benefit", to denounce the disbeliever.

safi-cedvel:39-39.t:
* I'rab:
(أم لكم أيمان) is like أم لكم كتاب «1»; (علينا) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أيمان) [Note: Or attached to a naʿt (adjective) of أيمان.]; (إلى يوم) attached to the "being settled" (istiqrār) which is the khabar (predicate) [Note: Or attached to بالغة.]; (إنّ لكم لما تحكمون) is like إنّ لكم ... لما تخيّرون «4» ...
The clause «لكم أيمان ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive. The clause «إنّ لكم لما تحكمون ...» has no grammatical position: response to the oath understood from the context of the verse لكم علينا أيمان ...
The clause «تحكمون ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (ما).

* Morphology:
(بالغة): feminine of بالغ, meaning firm and binding ... see verse (95) of Surat al-Māʾida,

safi-cedvel:40-40.t:
* I'rab:
(أيّهم) an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ) ... and (هم) is muḍāf ilayhi; (بذلك) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (زعيم), the reference being to the judgement by which the disbelievers judge; (زعيم) the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ أيّهم, nominative ...
The clause «سلهم ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «أيّهم ... زعيم» is in the position of accusative as the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the verb of asking, which is suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative أيّهم, and that with a preposition implied.

* Morphology:
(سلهم): its ʿayn — the hamza — has been deleted for lightness, optionally; and the deletion of the hamza in it entailed the deletion of the connecting hamza (hamzat al-waṣl) at its beginning. Its pattern is فلهم ... The hamza may be retained in this verb, and the connecting hamza restored, outside the verse ...

safi-cedvel:41-41.t:
* I'rab:
(أم لهم شركاء) is like أم لكم كتاب [Note: In verse (37) of the surah.]; (الفاء) linking the apodosis of an implied condition; (اللام) the lām of command; (بشركاء) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يأتوا); (كانوا) an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb in the position of jussive as protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ).
The clause «لهم شركاء ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «ليأتوا ...» is in the position of jussive as apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e.: if they have partners, let them bring ... [Note: Or: if they are truthful in what they say ... and the mentioned clause إن كانوا صادقين is explicative.].
The clause «إن كانوا ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive ... and the apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes.

safi-cedvel:42-43.t:
* I'rab:
(يوم) an adverb of time, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يأتوا) [Note: Or it is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being "remember" ...]; (عن ساق) the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of the verb يكشف; (الواو) in (يدعون) is the nāʾib fāʿil; (إلى السجود) attached to (يدعون); (الفاء) conjunction; (لا) negative ...
The clause «يكشف عن ساق ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «يدعون ...» is in the position of genitive, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause يكشف عن ساق.
The clause «لا يستطيعون ...» is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the clause يدعون.
43- (خاشعة) an accusative ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in (يدعون); (أبصارهم) the fāʿil (agent) of the active participle خاشعة, nominative; (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (قد) a particle of realisation (ḥarf taḥqīq); (إلى السجود) attached to the second (يدعون); (الواو) circumstantial ...
The clause «ترهقهم ذلّة ...» is in the position of accusative as an emphasising ḥāl of the nāʾib fāʿil of يدعون.
The clause «قد كانوا ...» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl [Note: Or an emphasising resumption of the content of what preceded.].
The clause «يدعون» (the second) is in the position of accusative as khabar (predicate) of كانوا.
The clause «هم سالمون ...» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of the pronoun in the second (يدعون).

* Morphology:
(سالمون): plural of سالم, active participle of the triliteral سلم, of the class of فرح. Its pattern is فاعل.

* Rhetoric:
Representative metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-tamthīliyya): in His words «يَوْمَ يُكْشَفُ عَنْ ساقٍ».
Uncovering it and tucking up from it is a proverbial image for the severity of a matter and the difficulty of an affair, because whoever falls into something that requires earnest effort tucks up [Translator's note: his garment] from his shin.
Indefiniteness (al-tankīr): in His word «ساق».
ساق came indefinite to indicate that it is a matter indeterminate in its severity, unfamiliar, outside the ordinary.
The secret of attributing humility to the eyes: in His words «خاشِعَةً أَبْصارُهُمْ».
That is because its effect appears in them, for what is in the heart is known from the eye; so it is a rational (ʿaqlī) figure of speech.

safi-cedvel:44-45.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) linking the apodosis of an implied condition; (الواو) conjunction; (من) a relative in the position of accusative, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the first-person pronoun in (ذرني); (بهذا) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يكذّب); (الحديث) a badal (substitute) of the demonstrative, genitive — or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) to it; (السين) for futurity; (حيث) an adverbial noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma, in the position of genitive, attached to (نستدرجهم); (لا) negative.
The clause «ذرني ...» has no grammatical position: apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e.: if their states are thus, then leave Me ...
The clause «يكذّب ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (من).
The clause «سنستدرجهم ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «لا يعلمون ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
45- (الواو) conjunction; (لهم) attached to (أملي) ...
The clause «أملي لهم ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause سنستدرجهم.
The clause «إنّ كيدي متين» has no grammatical position: causal (taʿlīliyya) ...

* Rhetoric:
Synecdoche / non-metaphorical figure (al-majāz al-mursal): in His words «وَأُمْلِي لَهُمْ إِنَّ كَيْدِي مَتِينٌ».
He called His granting them respite, and the succession of favours and bounties upon them, a "plot" because it is the cause of entanglement and destruction; for the reality of a plot is a kind of stratagem, because it is in its form: He, Glorified is He, does with them what is outwardly a benefit to them, while what He, Mighty and Majestic, intends by it is harm, because of what He knows of the vileness of their nature and their persistence in disbelief and ingratitude.

safi-cedvel:46-46.t:
* I'rab:
(أم) disconnected (munqaṭiʿa), in the sense of بل and the hamza; (الفاء) causal (taʿlīliyya); (من مغرم) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (مثقلون) ...
The clause «تسألهم ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «هم ... مثقلون» has no grammatical position: causal.

safi-cedvel:47-47.t:
* I'rab:
(أم) like the preceding one [Note: In the previous verse (46).]; (عندهم) an accusative adverb, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a fronted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (الغيب); (الفاء) conjunction.
The clause «عندهم الغيب ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «هم يكتبون ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the resumptive clause.
The clause «يكتبون ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم).

safi-cedvel:48-50.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) linking the apodosis of an implied condition; (لحكم) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (اصبر) by its being made to carry (taḍmīn) the meaning of اخضع "submit"; (الواو) conjunction; (لا) a prohibitive, jussive-governing particle; (كصاحب) attached to the khabar (predicate) of تكن, with a muḍāf omitted [Note: I.e. let not your state be like the state of the companion of the fish.]; (إذ) an adverb in the position of accusative, attached to the implied muḍāf, i.e. like the state of the companion of the fish at the time of his calling out; (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya).
The clause «اصبر ...» is in the position of jussive as apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e.: if you fall into distress, then be patient ...
The clause «لا تكن ...» is in the position of jussive, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause اصبر.
The clause «نادى ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «هو مكظوم» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).
49- (لولا) a non-jussive conditional particle; (أن) an infinitival particle; (تداركه) an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb), from which one of the two tāʾs has been deleted [Note: Or it is a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa; the verb came masculine — which is permissible — because the fāʿil (agent) is figuratively feminine.], and (الهاء) is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (من ربّه) attached to a naʿt (adjective) of (نعمة); (اللام) linking the apodosis of لولا; (بالعراء) attached to (نبذ), and (الباء) is locative (li-l-ẓarf); (الواو) circumstantial.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تداركه ...) is in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject) ... and the khabar is omitted.
The clause «لولا (تدارك) نعمة ربّه ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «تداركه نعمة ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (أن).
The clause «نبذ ...» has no grammatical position: apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «هو مذموم ...» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl.
50- (الفاء) conjunction in both places; (من الصالحين) attached to an omitted second mafʿūl bihi.
The clause «اجتباه ربّه ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause لولا أن ...
The clause «جعله من الصالحين» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause اجتباه.

* Morphology:
(48) مكظوم: passive participle of the triliteral كظم. Its pattern is مفعول.

* Rhetoric:
Al-majāz al-mursal (non-metaphorical figure): in His words «وَهُوَ مَذْمُومٌ».
A majāz mursal, because blame (lawm) is in reality a cause of censure (dhamm); so the relation is causality.

safi-cedvel:51-52.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (إن) lightened from the heavy one, necessarily left ungoverning (muhmala); (اللام) is the distinguishing lām (al-fāriqa); (بأبصارهم) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يزلقونك); (لمّا) an adverb in the sense of "when", containing the meaning of condition, in the position of accusative, attached to the implied apodosis; (الواو) conjunction; (اللام) the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), for emphasis [Translator's note: the source prints «للتوحيد» ("for unification"), evidently a misprint for «للتوكيد» ("for emphasis"), which is translated.] ...
The clause «يكاد الذين ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive ...
The clause «كفروا ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين). The clause «يزلقونك ...» is in the position of accusative as khabar (predicate) of يكاد. The clause «سمعوا ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi ... and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes, i.e. they almost made you slip.
The clause «يقولون ...» is in the position of accusative, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause يزلقونك. The clause «إنّه لمجنون» is in the position of accusative as the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl).
52- (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (ما) negative, ungoverning (muhmala); (إلّا) for restriction (ḥaṣr); (للعالمين) attached to (ذكر) [Note: Or attached to a naʿt (adjective) of ذكر.].
The clause «ما هو إلّا ذكر ...» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

semin-durr:1-1.t:
His saying: {ن}: like His saying {ص والقرآن} [Ṣād: 1], and the answer to the oath is the negated clause after it. Some claimed that it is the name of a fish and that it is the singular of النِّينان; some that it is the name of the inkwell; and some that it is the name of a tablet written upon. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "As for their saying that it is the inkwell, I do not know whether it is a linguistic or a legal coinage. And if it is a name for the inkwell, it must be either a generic noun or a proper name. If it is generic, where is the i'rab and the tanwīn? And if it is a proper name, where is the i'rab? Whichever it is, it must have a place in the construction of the discourse, because if you make it something sworn by, then — if it is generic — you must put it in the genitive and give it tanwīn, and the oath would be by an indefinite, unknown inkwell, as if it were said: 'By an inkwell, and the Pen'; and if it is a proper name, you must make it a triptote and put it in the genitive, or make it a diptote and give it fatḥa because of being a proper name and feminine. Likewise the interpretation as the fish: either one of the fishes (al-nīnān) is meant by it, or it is made a proper name for the Bahamūt that they claim. The interpretation as the tablet of light or of gold, and as the river in Paradise, is similar to that." What Abū al-Qāsim adduced here is among the fine points of the science of i'rab, and few master it.
The majority read «ن» with the nūn quiescent, like its counterparts. Ibn ʿĀmir, al-Kisāʾī and Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim, without disagreement, and Warsh, with disagreement from him, assimilated the nūn into the wāw; the rest pronounced it clearly. From those who assimilated, both nasalisation (ghunna) and its absence are transmitted. Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḥasan, Abū al-Sammāl and Ibn Abī Isḥāq read it with the nūn vowelled with kasra; and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and ʿĪsā, with disagreement from him, with fatḥa. The first [the kasra] is because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. It may not be a genitive by the oath — the preposition being dropped while its sign [Translator's note: the text has «علمُه», evidently for «عملُه», "its effect"] remains, as in their saying «اللَّهِ لأفعلَنَّ» ("By Allah, I shall surely do") — for two reasons. The first: that this is restricted to the exalted Name of Majesty and rare elsewhere. The second: that it would then have had to take tanwīn. Nor is it good to say that it is a diptote in view of the feminine gender of the sūra, because then the genitive would not appear in it by kasra at all.
As for the fatḥa, it admits three views. The first: that it is indeclinability (bināʾ), preferred over the basic [kasra] for lightness, as in أينَ and كيفَ. The second: that it is a genitive by an implied preposition of oath, according to a weak dialect — this has preceded in the reading «فالحقِّ والحقِّ» [Ṣād: 84] with «الحقِّ» in the genitive — and it was made a diptote in view of the sūra. The third: that it is accusative by an omitted verb, i.e. "Recite Nūn!", and then He began an oath with His saying «والقلمِ»; or it is accusative after the omission of the particle of oath, as in his saying:
4290 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ...
فذاكَ أمانةَ اللَّهِ الثِّريدُ
(… that, by the trust of Allah, is the tharīd.)
and it was made a diptote for the reason given. This is the best, because «والقلمِ» is conjoined to its position.
His saying: {وَمَا يَسْطُرُونَ}: «ما» is a relative, either nominal or particle [i.e. maṣdariyya], i.e. "and what they write of books" — they being the scribes or the recording angels — or "and their writing". The pronoun refers back to whoever writes, because the context indicates him, and because the instrument written with has been mentioned. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It may be that by the Pen its owners are meant, so the pronoun in «يَسْطُرون» is for them" — meaning that it then becomes like His saying {أَوْ كَظُلُمَاتٍ فِي بَحْرٍ لُّجِّيٍّ يَغْشَاهُ} [al-Nūr: 40], its implied form being "or like one in darknesses", so the pronoun in «يَغْشاه» refers back to the omitted «ذي».

semin-durr:2-2.t:
His saying: {بِنِعْمَةِ رَبِّكَ}: the counterpart of this has preceded in al-Ṭūr, at His saying {فَذَكِّرْ فَمَآ أَنتَ بِنِعْمَةِ رَبِّكَ بِكَاهِنٍ} [al-Ṭūr: 29], with its verification. However, al-Zamakhsharī said here: "If you say: to what is the bāʾ in «بنعمة ربك» attached, and what is its position? I say: it is attached to «مجنون» negated, just as it is attached to «عاقل» affirmed, as in your saying 'You, by the grace of Allah, are sane' — affirmation and negation being equal in this, as they are equal in your saying 'Zayd struck ʿAmr' and 'Zayd did not strike ʿAmr': you make the verb govern, negated and affirmed, in one and the same way. Its position is the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), as if He said: you are not mad, being favoured with that. And the bāʾ does not prevent «مجنون» from governing what precedes it, because it is redundant, to emphasise the negation."
The Shaykh said: "What al-Zamakhsharī held — that the bāʾ is attached to «مجنون» and that it is in the position of a ḥāl — needs reflection. That is because when negation is directed at a predicate that has a governed element, there are two ways. One: that the negation is directed at that governed element only. The other: that the negation is directed at the predicate, so its governed element is negated by its being negated. The explanation of that: you say 'Zayd is not standing hurriedly'; what comes first to the mind is that his hurrying is negated, not his standing, so he has stood without hurrying. The other way: that his standing is negated, and so his hurrying is negated, i.e. no standing, so no hurrying. With what we have established, al-Zamakhsharī's saying cannot hold in any way; rather it leads to what may not be uttered regarding the one protected from error (al-maʿṣūm)." End of quote.
The Shaykh chose that «بنعمة» be an oath interposed between the subject and the predicate, by way of emphasis, stress and intensification in negating the blameworthy description. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "«بنعمةِ ربِّك» is parenthetical, as you say to a person: 'You, praise be to Allah, are excellent'." He [the Shaykh] said: "He did not explain to what the bāʾ in «بنعمة» is attached." I say: what the bāʾ is attached to in this kind is the meaning of the content of the clause, negated or affirmed, as if it were said: that has been negated of you by the praise of Allah — the bāʾ being causal — and excellence has been established for you by the praise of Allah the Exalted. As for the example he mentioned, the bāʾ in it is attached to the word «فاضل». The author of al-Muntakhab inclined to this, saying: "The meaning is: madness has been negated of you by the grace of your Lord. It was also said: its meaning is 'You are not mad, and the grace belongs to your Lord', as in their saying 'Glory be to You, O Allah, and with Your praise', i.e. and the praise belongs to Allah. Of this is the saying of Labīd:
4291 - وأُفْرِدْتُ في الدنيا بفَقْدِ عشيرتي ... وفارقني جارٌ بأَرْبَدَ نافِعُ
(I have been left alone in the world by the loss of my kinsmen, and a beneficial neighbour has parted from me — Arbad.)
i.e. and he is Arbad." This is not an explanation of i'rab but an explanation of meaning.

semin-durr:6-6.t: His saying: {بِأَيِّكُمُ المفتون}: there are four views on it. The first: that the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida) on the mubtadaʾ (subject), the implied form being: "which of you is the afflicted one", and it was added as it is added in such as «بحَسْبك زيدٌ» ("Zayd is sufficient for you"). Qatāda and Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar ibn al-Muthannā held this; but it is weak inasmuch as the bāʾ is not added to the mubtadaʾ except in «حَسْبُك» only. The second: that the bāʾ is in the sense of «في», so it is locative, as in your saying «زيدٌ بالبصرة» ("Zayd is in Basra"), i.e. in it; the meaning is: in which group and party of you is the afflicted one. Mujāhid and al-Farrāʾ held this, and it is supported by the reading of Ibn Abī ʿAbla «في أيِّكم». The third: that it is on the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "with which of you is the affliction of the afflicted one", the muḍāf being omitted and the muḍāf ilayhi put in its place. Al-Akhfash held this, and the bāʾ is then causal. The fourth: that «المفتون» is a maṣdar (verbal noun) that came on the mafʿūl pattern, like المَعْقول and المسيور, the implied form being: "with which of you is the affliction (الفُتون)". On the first view, the discourse is complete at His saying «ويُبْصِرون», and His saying «بأيِّكم المفْتون» begins anew; on the views after it, the bāʾ is attached to what precedes it, and one does not pause at «يُبْصِرون». On the first three views, «المفتون» is a passive participle according to its basic form; on the fourth view it is a maṣdar. It ought to be said that the discourse is complete only at His saying «المفتون», whether the bāʾ is said to be redundant or not, because His saying «فَسَتُبْصِرُ ويُبْصرون» is suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative after it, since it is a verb in the sense of seeing, and visual seeing is suspended, according to the correct view, as shown by their saying «أما ترى أيُّ بَرْقٍ ههنا» ("Do you not see what lightning is here?"); and so it is with الإبصار, because it is seeing with the eye. So on the view that the bāʾ is redundant, the interrogative clause is in the position of the accusative, because it stands in the place of the object of seeing.

semin-durr:9-9.t:
His saying: {فَيُدْهِنُونَ}: what is well known in the reading of people and in their maṣāḥif is «فيُدْهِنون», with the nūn of the nominative retained. There are two views on it. The first: that it is conjoined to «تُدْهِنُ», so it enters into the domain of «لو». The second: that it is the khabar (predicate) of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. so they compromise. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: why was «فَيُدْهِنون» put in the nominative and not in the accusative by an implied «أَنْ», it being the answer to the wish? I say: it has been turned to another path, namely that it was made the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. so they compromise, as in His saying {فَمَن يُؤْمِن بِرَبِّهِ فَلاَ يَخَافُ بَخْساً}, in the sense: they wished that you would compromise, so they would compromise then; or: they wished for your compromising, so they are now compromising because of their hope of your compromising. Sībawayh said: 'Hārūn claimed that in some maṣāḥif it is «وَدُّوا لو تُدْهِنُ فيُدِهنوا»'." End of quote.
Regarding its accusative, as found in some maṣāḥif, there are two views. The first: that it is conjoined by supposition (ʿaṭf ʿalā al-tawahhum), as if he supposed that «أَنْ» had been pronounced and put the verb in the accusative on this supposition; this is possible only on the view that «لو» is maṣdariyya, about which there is a disagreement that has passed with verification in al-Baqara. The second: that it is accusative as the answer to the wish understood from «وَدَّ». What is apparent is that «لو» here is the particle for what would have happened because of the happening of something else, and that its answer is omitted; and the object of the wishing is also omitted, its implied form being "they wished for your compromising", «إدْهانَك» being omitted because «لو» and what follows it indicate it. The implied form of the answer is: they would have been pleased with that.

semin-durr:10-10.t:
His saying: {مَّهِينٍ هَمَّازٍ}: the explanation of «مهين» has preceded in al-Zukhruf. And «الهمَّاز» is an intensive form from الهَمْز, which in the language is striking by jabbing with the hand, a stick and the like; it was borrowed for the fault-finder who finds fault with people, as if he strikes them. And «النَّميم»: it was said to be a maṣdar (verbal noun), like النميمة; and it was said to be its plural, i.e. a collective noun, like تمرة and تمر. It is the conveying of speech that distresses the one who hears it and stirs up enmity between people. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "النميم and النَّميمة mean slandering (al-siʿāya); one of the Arabs recited to me:
4292 - تَشَبَّبي تَشَبُّبَ النَّميمهْ ... تَمشْي بها زَهْراً إلى تميمهْ
(Blaze up as slander blazes up, carried openly to Tamīma.)"
And «المَشَّاء» is an intensive form from المَشْي, i.e. he goes about much with slander among people. And «العُتُلّ» is the one who drags (yaʿtilu) people, i.e. carries them off and pulls them to what they hate, of imprisonment and beating; from it is {خُذُوهُ فاعتلوه} [al-Dukhān: 47]. It was said: العُتُلّ is the one who is fierce in dispute. Abū ʿUbayda said: "It is the obscene, base one", and he recited:
4293 - بعُتُلٍّ مِنْ الرِّجالِ زَنِيمٍ ... غيرِ ذي نَجْدةٍ وغيرِ كريمِ
(… with a coarse man, of no known lineage, without valour and without nobility.)
And it was said: the coarse, harsh one. One says عَتَلْتُه and عَتَنْتُه, with lām and with nūn; Yaʿqūb transmitted it. And «الزنيم» is the pretender (al-daʿī) who is attributed to a people of whom he is not. Ḥassān said:
4294 - زَنيمٌ تَداعاه الرجالُ زيادةً ... كما زِيْدَ في عَرْضِ الأديمِ الأكارِعُ
(An adopted hanger-on whom men claimed as an extra, as the shanks are added onto the breadth of a hide.)
He also said:
4295 - وأنتَ زَنيمٌ نِيْطَ في آل هاشمٍ ... كما نِيْطَ خلفَ الرَّاكبِ القَدَحُ الفَرْدُ
(You are a hanger-on attached to the family of Hāshim, as the lone cup is tied behind the rider.)
Its origin is from الزَّنَمَة: what remains of the skin of a goat hanging from its throat, left when cutting; so it was borrowed for the pretender, because he is like something hung onto what he is not of. Al-Ḥasan read «عُتُلٌّ» in the nominative, as "he is عُتُلٌّ". By right what follows it should also be read in the nominative, because they said regarding cutting off [the adjectives] that one starts with following [the case] and then cuts off, not the reverse. His saying «بعد ذلك» means: after what we have described him with. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "This order is only in the speech of the describer, not in the occurrence of those qualities in the one described [Translator's note: the text has «المصوف», evidently for «الموصوف»]; otherwise his being عُتُلّ comes before his being one who withholds good." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«بعد ذلك»: after what has been counted against him of vices and defects." Then he said: "He made his harshness and his false claim [of lineage] the more serious faults, because when his nature is coarse and harsh, his heart hardens and he dares to commit every sin."

semin-durr:14-14.t:
His saying: {أَن كَانَ}: the majority read the hamza of «أنْ» with fatḥa; then they differed after that. Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥamza and Abū Bakr read it as a question, and the rest of the Seven as a statement. Those who read it as a question follow their principles: pronouncing [the hamza] fully or easing it, and inserting an alif between the two hamzas or not. I must explain it to you to make the matter easy for you, so I say, and success is from Allah: Ḥamza and Abū Bakr read it with both hamzas pronounced fully and without inserting an alif between them, and this is their principle.
Ibn Dhakwān read it with the second eased and without inserting an alif; and Hishām with the easing mentioned, except that he inserted an alif between them. So each of the two has departed from his principle. As for Ibn Dhakwān: he pronounces both hamzas fully, yet he eased the second here. As for Hishām: his principle is to apply two ways to the second in this kind — pronouncing it fully, like his companion, and easing it — yet he kept to easing here. As for inserting the alif, he is according to his principle in it, as preceded at the beginning of al-Baqara.
Nāfiʿ, in the transmission of al-Zubaydī from him, read «إنْ كان» with the hamza vowelled with kasra, as a condition.
As for the reading «أَنْ كان» with fatḥa as a statement, there are four views on it. The first: that it is the maṣdariyya «أنْ», in the position of the mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), in the genitive by an implied lām, the lām being attached to the verb of prohibition, i.e. do not obey one whose qualities these are because he is wealthy and has sons. The second: that it is attached to «عُتُلّ», even though it has been described [by adjectives] — al-Fārisī said this; this is not permissible according to the Basrans, but it seems al-Fārisī overlooked it in the case of a preposition phrase. The third: that it is attached to «زنيم», especially according to whoever explains it as [one of] vile deeds. The fourth: that it is attached to an omitted element indicated by the conditional clause after it, its implied form being: because he is wealthy and supported by sons, he denied Our signs — al-Zamakhsharī said this. He said: "«قال», which is the answer of «إذا», does not govern it, because what follows the condition does not govern what precedes it; but rather the meaning of denial that the clause indicates [governs it]." Makkī said, and Abū al-Baqāʾ followed him: "The governor may not be «تُتْلى», because what follows «إذا» does not govern what precedes it, since «إذا» is annexed to clauses, and the muḍāf ilayhi does not govern what precedes the muḍāf." End of quote. This gives the impression that the impediment to that is only what he mentioned, whereas the impediment is a matter of meaning: even if this impediment he mentioned were absent, it would be excluded from the side of meaning — namely that it is not fitting to give his being possessed of wealth and sons as the reason for the recitation of Allah's signs to him.
As for the reading «أَأَنْ كان» as a question, there are two views on it. The first: that it is attached to an implied element indicated by what precedes it, i.e. will you obey him because he is …, or: is there to be obedience because he is …? The second: that it is attached to an implied element [indicated by] [Translator's note: the words «يدلّ» appear to have dropped from the text here] what follows it, i.e. because he is such-and-such, he denied and rejected.
As for the reading «إنْ» with kasra, it is as a condition, and its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is implied, its implied form being: if he is such-and-such, he disbelieves and rejects — what follows it indicates it. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The condition is for the one addressed, i.e. do not obey every habitual swearer while stipulating his affluence; because if he obeys the unbeliever for his wealth, it is as if he made wealth a condition of obedience. Like the turning of the condition to the one addressed is the turning of hope to him in His saying {لَّعَلَّهُ يَتَذَكَّرُ} [Ṭāhā: 44]." The Shaykh made it a case of a condition entering upon a condition, meaning «إنْ» and «إذا», except that he said: "They are not among the conditions whose occurrence is ordered in sequence", and he made it a counterpart of the saying of Ibn Durayd:
4296 - فإنْ عَثَرْتُ بعدَها إنْ وَأَلَتْ ... نفسيَ مِنْ هاتا فقولا لا لَعا
(If I stumble after it — if my soul escapes from this one — then say: "No recovery!")
He said: "Because what drives [him] to reflecting [Translator's note: so in the text; the sense seems to require "away from reflecting" or "to not reflecting"] on the signs of Allah is his being possessed of wealth and sons, while his heart is occupied with that, heedless of consideration; this world has taken hold of him and made him insolent."
Al-Ḥasan read it as a question, and it is a question of reproach and rebuke for his saying "The Quran is the legends of the ancients" when the signs of Allah were recited to him.

semin-durr:16-16.t:
His saying: {سَنَسِمُهُ}: i.e. We will put on him a brand (سِمَة), i.e. a mark by which he will be known. Jarīr said:
4297 - لَمَّا وَضَعْتُ على الفرزدقِ مِيْسَمي ... وعلى البَعيثِ جَدَعْتُ أَنْفَ الأخطلِ
(When I set my branding iron on al-Farazdaq and on al-Baʿīth, I cut off the nose of al-Akhṭal.)
And «الخُرْطُوم» is the nose; here it stands for the whole face, of [the category of] expressing the whole by the part, because it is the most prominent and highest thing in it. الخُرْطوم is also wine; it seems to be a metaphor for it, because al-Shantamarī said: "It is the wine when it first comes out of the jar", so it was made like the nose, since it is the first thing that appears of the face. So الخرطوم is not wine absolutely. Of the use of الخُرْطوم in the sense of wine is the saying of ʿAlqama ibn ʿAbada:
4298 - قد أَشْهَدُ الشَّرْبَ، فيهم مُزْهِرٌ زَئِمٌ ... والقومُ تصرَعُهمْ صَهْباءُ خُرْطومُ
(I have attended the drinking party, among them a lute-player with a resonant lute, while the people are felled by a reddish, first-drawn wine.)
And al-Naḍr ibn Shumayl recited:
4299 - تَظَلُّ يومَك في لهو وفي لَعِبٍ ... وأنتَ بالليل شَرَّابُ الخَراطيمِ
(You spend your day in diversion and play, and at night you are a drinker of choice wines.)
Al-Naḍr said: "الخُرطوم in the verse is wine, and what is meant is: We will flog him for drinking it." People have considered this interpretation far-fetched.

semin-durr:17-17.t: His saying: {مُصْبِحِينَ}: this is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the agent of «لَيَصْرِمُنَّها», and it is from the complete (tāmma) «أصبح», i.e. entering upon the morning, as in His saying the Exalted {وَإِنَّكُمْ لَّتَمُرُّونَ عَلَيْهِمْ مُّصْبِحِينَ} [al-Ṣāffāt: 137], and their saying: "If you hear of the smith's night travel, know that he will be arriving in the morning." The kāf in «كما» is in the position of the accusative as the adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. We tested them with a testing like the one with which We tested. And «ما» is maṣdariyya or in the sense of «الذين». And «إذ» is accusative by «بَلَوْنا». And «لَيَصْرِمنُّها» is the answer to the oath; it came in a form different from their actual wording — had it come according to it, it would have been said لَنَصْرِمُنَّها, with the nūn of the speakers.

semin-durr:18-18.t: His saying: {وَلاَ يَسْتَثْنُونَ}: this is resumptive (mustaʾnafa). Its being a ḥāl (circumstantial) is weak, inasmuch as the imperfect negated by «لا» is like the affirmed one in that the wāw does not enter upon it; and implying a mubtadaʾ (subject) before it, as in their saying «قمتُ وأَصُكُّ عينَه» ("I stood up, and I strike his eye"), is unnecessary. The meaning of «لا يَسْتَثْنُون» is: they do not turn back (yathnūn) their resolve on depriving [the poor]. It was also said: they do not say "If Allah wills". It was called an exception (istithnāʾ) although it is a condition, because the meaning of "I shall surely go out, if Allah wills" and "I shall not go out unless Allah wills" is one — al-Zamakhsharī said this.

semin-durr:19-19.t:
His saying: {طَآئِفٌ}: that is, a destruction or a calamity, "circling" (ṭāʾif). The word ṭāʾif has come to be used predominantly for evil. Al-Farrāʾ said: "It is the affair that comes by night." This was refuted by His saying: {إِذَا مَسَّهُمْ طَائِفٌ مِّنَ الشيطان} [al-Aʿrāf: 201], since that is restricted to neither night nor day. Al-Nakhaʿī read «طَيْفٌ».
