The discussion of these two descriptions has already been given in al-Aʿrāf. And «مِن رَّبِّكَ» may be attached to «طاف», or it may be attached to an omitted element as an adjective of «طائف». Al-ṣirām is the cutting of the date-palms (picking their fruit). The root basically indicates cutting, and from it come al-ṣurm and al-ṣarm, with ḍamma and fatḥa, meaning severance. Imruʾ al-Qays said:
4300 - أفاطمُ مَهْلاً بعضَ هذا التدلُّلِ ... وإن كُنْتِ قد أَزْمَعْتِ صَرْمي فأَجْملي
(O Fāṭima, gently, a little of this coquetry; and if you have resolved to cut me off, then do it gracefully.)
From it also comes al-ṣarīma, which is a piece cut off from the sand. He said:
4301 - وبالصَّرِيْمَةِ منهم مَنْزِلٌ خَلِقٌ ... عافٍ تَغَيَّرِ إلاَّ النؤيُ والوَتِدُ
(And at al-Ṣarīma, of their dwelling, there is a worn-out abode, effaced and changed, except for the trench and the tent-peg.)
Al-ṣārim is the cutting, sharp one, and a she-camel muṣarramah means one whose milk has been cut off. "The month and the year were cut off (inṣarama)" means that their ending drew near. And "aṣrama" means his condition turned bad, as if his good fortune had been cut off. As for His saying «كالصريم», it was said that it refers to the trees whose fruit has been cut off.
And it was said: it means "like the night", because the night is called al-ṣarīm for its blackness. Al-ṣarīm is also the day. And it was said: the dawn; so it is one of the words with opposite meanings (aḍdād). Shamir said: al-ṣarīm is the night and al-ṣarīm is the day, because this is cut off from that and that from this. It was said: it is ashes, in the dialect of Khuzayma; Ibn ʿAbbās said this. It was said: al-ṣarīm is a well-known stretch of sand in Yemen that grows nothing. And in the exegesis: their garden became like that. It is also reported that it was uprooted and set down where al-Ṭāʾif is today; and for that reason al-Ṭāʾif, which is in the Hijaz today, was named after it.

semin-durr:22-22.t:
His saying: {أَنِ اغدوا}: it may be the maṣdar-forming «أَنْ» (that is, "they called to one another with these words"), and it may be the explicative «أَنْ», because what precedes it has the sense of saying. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: why was it not said 'Go early to your tilth', and what is the meaning of «على»? I say: since going out early to it was in order to cut and harvest it, it was a going early upon it, as you say, 'the enemy went early upon them'. It is also possible that «الغدو» is made to include the meaning of coming forward, as in their saying: 'The dish is brought to them in the morning and in the evening.'" End of quotation. So he made «غدا» originally transitive by means of «إلى», and so needed an interpretation to explain its transitivity by «على». There is something questionable in this, since its transitivity by «على» occurs in more than one place, such as his saying:
4302 - وقد أَغْدُو على ثُبَةٍ كِرامٍ ... نَشاوى واجِدين لِما نشاءُ
(And I go early upon a noble company, merry, finding whatever we wish.)
/ And if they have made its synonym transitive by «على», then let them make it transitive by it as well. Its synonym is «بَكَرَ»: you say "I went early upon him" with bakartu ʿalayhi and ghadawtu ʿalayhi in a single sense. He said:
4303 - بَكَرْتُ عليه غُدْوَةً فَرَأَيْتُه ... قُعُوداً لديهِ بالصَّريمِ عَواذِلُهْ
(I went early to him in the morning and saw him, with his female blamers sitting by him at al-Ṣarīm.)
And {إِن كُنتُمْ صَارِمِينَ}: its apodosis is omitted, that is, "then go early". And ṣārimīn means cutters, harvesters. It was also said: resolute in determination, from your saying "a sharp sword" (sayf ṣārim).

semin-durr:23-23.t: His saying: {وَهُمْ يَتَخَافَتُونَ}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause from the agent of «انطلَقُوا».

semin-durr:24-24.t: His saying: {أَن لاَّ يَدْخُلَنَّهَا}: it may be the maṣdar-forming «أَنْ» (that is, "they were whispering with these words", meaning that some of them said it to others), and it may be the explicative «أَنْ». ʿAbd Allāh and Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «لا يَدْخُلُها» with the omission of «أَنْ», either on the implication of saying, as is the doctrine of the Basrans, or on treating «يتخافتون» as having the same status (as saying), as is the view of the Kufans.

semin-durr:25-25.t:
His saying: {على حَرْدٍ قَادِرِينَ}: «قادرين» may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of «غَدَوْا», with «على حَرْدٍ» attached to it; or «على حَرْدٍ» may be the ḥāl, with «قادرين» either a second ḥāl or a ḥāl from the pronoun of the first ḥāl.
As for al-ḥard, there are many opinions about it. It was said: anger and rage. A verse by al-Ashhab ibn Rumayla was recited:
4304 - أُسُوْدُ شَرىً لاقَتْ أُسُودَ خَفِيَّةٍ ... تَساقَوْا على حَرْدٍ دماءَ الأساوِدِ
(Lions of Sharā met the lions of Khafiyya; in rage they gave one another the blood of the serpents to drink.)
It was said that the like of it is the saying of another:
4305 - إذا جِيادُ الخيل جاءتَ تَرْدي ... مملوءَةً مِنْ غَضَبٍ وحَرْد
(When the thoroughbred horses came galloping, filled with anger and ḥard.)
He joined them (the two words) because the two expressions differ, as in his saying:
4306 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... وأَلْفى قولَها كَذِباً ومَيْنا
(... and he found her speech to be falsehood and lying.)
And it was said: prevention. It is from "the camels became ḥārid", meaning their milk became scanty, and "the year became ḥārid", meaning its rain became scanty; Abū ʿUbayd and al-Qutaybī said this. It is said ḥarida, with kasra, yaḥradu ḥardan, and it may be vowelled with fatḥa, so one says ḥaradan, and he is ḥardān and ḥārid. It is said "a ḥārid lion" and "ḥawārid lions". It was said: al-ḥard and al-ḥarad mean separation. It is said ḥarada, with fatḥa, yaḥrudu, with ḍamma, ḥurūdan and ḥardan and ḥaradan: he withdrew; and from it comes "a ḥārid star", that is, one that is solitary. Al-Aṣmaʿī said: "It is the dialect of Hudhayl." And it was said: al-ḥard means intention. It is said ḥarada yaḥridu ḥardaka, meaning "he intended your intention", and from it:
4307 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ...
يَحْرِدُ حَرْدَ الجنَّةِ المُغِلَّهْ
(... he heads for it as one heads for the fruitful garden.)
The noble verse has been interpreted by all that I have mentioned. And it was said: al-Ḥard is the name of their garden itself; al-Suddī said this. And it was said: the name of their village; al-Azharī said this. In both there is a very great remoteness. And «قادرين» is either from qudra (power), which is the obvious sense, or from taqdīr (straitening), which is narrowing, that is, "straitening the poor". In the exegesis there is a story that clarifies what I have mentioned.

semin-durr:33-33.t: His saying: {كَذَلِكَ العذاب}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is placed first; that is, "the like of that punishment is the punishment of this world, while the punishment of the Hereafter is greater than it."

semin-durr:34-34.t: His saying: {عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ}: it may be accusative by the sense of settledness (istiqrār), and it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «جَنَّات».

semin-durr:38-38.t: His saying: {إِنَّ لَكُمْ فِيهِ}: the majority read it with kasra on the hamza. There are three possibilities in it. The first: it is governed by «تَدْرُسون», that is, "you study in the Book that you shall have what you choose", and when the lām entered, the hamza was given kasra. The second: it is by way of quoting what is studied exactly as it is, like His saying: {وَتَرَكْنَا عَلَيْهِ فِي الآخرين سَلاَمٌ على نُوحٍ فِي العالمين} [al-Ṣāffāt: 78-79]. Al-Zamakhsharī stated both; and the difference between the two possibilities is hard to see. He said: "takhayyara al-shayʾ and ikhtārahu means he took its best, like tanakhkhalahu and intakhalahu, he took what was sifted from it." The third: it is resumptive, in the sense "if you have a book, then in it you have something to choose from." Ṭalḥa and al-Ḍaḥḥāk read «أنَّ لكم» with fatḥa on the hamza, and it is then governed by «تَدْرُسُون» in the accusative, except that it contains the addition of the lām of emphasis; and this is parallel to the reading {إِلاَّ إِنَّهُمْ لَيَأْكُلُونَ} [al-Furqān: 20] with fatḥa. Al-Aʿraj read «أإنَّ لكم» in both places, as a question.

semin-durr:39-39.t:
His saying: {بَالِغَةٌ}: the majority read it in the nominative, as a naʿt (adjective) of «أَيْمانٌ»; and «إلى يوم» is attached to what «لكم» is attached to, namely settledness (istiqrār), that is, "established for you until the day of"; or it is attached to «بالغة», that is, "reaching to that day and ending at it."
Zayd ibn ʿAlī and al-Ḥasan read it in the accusative. It was said: as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «أيمان», because it has been made specific by the operation or by the description. And it was said: from the pronoun in «علينا», if we make it an adjective of «أَيْمان».
And His saying: {إِنَّ لَكُمْ لَمَا تَحْكُمُونَ} is the answer to the oath in His saying «أَيْمان», because it has the sense of oaths. And «أيُّهم» suspends the effect of «سَلْهُمْ» (ta'līq), and «بذلك» is attached to «زعيمٌ», that is, a guarantor and surety. It has already been mentioned that «سأل» can be suspended, since it is a cause of knowledge. Originally it takes its object with ʿan or with the bāʾ, as in His saying: {فَسْئَلْ بِهِ خَبِيراً} [al-Furqān: 59] [and his saying:] 4308 - فإنْ تَسْألوني بالنساء. . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(If you ask me about women ...)
So the clause is in the position of the accusative after the dropping of the preposition, as you have learned its explanation more than once. ʿAbd Allāh read: «أم لهم شِركٌ، فليَأْتوا بشِرْكِهم», using the verbal noun.

semin-durr:42-42.t:
His saying: {يَوْمَ يُكْشَفُ}: it is accusative by His saying «فَلْيَأْتُوا», or by the implication of "remember", in which case it is a direct object; or by an omitted element, in which case it is an adverbial: "on the day when it is uncovered, such and such will be"; or by «خاشعة», as Abū al-Baqāʾ said, and there is remoteness in this. And «عن ساقٍ» stands in the place of the agent. Ibn Masʿūd and Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «يَكْشِفُ» with yāʾ, active, the agent being Allah. Ibn ʿAbbās and ʿAbd Allāh also read «نكشِفُ» with kasra on the shīn and nūn. From Ibn ʿAbbās there is also «تَكْشِفُ» with tāʾ, active, that is, the hardship and the Hour. And from him likewise it is passive, and it is / problematic, because the feminine has no sense here, unless it is said that the object is latent, that is, "it is uncovered", meaning the hardship.
His saying: {عَن سَاقٍ}, that is, "it uncovers its shin"; for that reason al-Zamakhsharī said: "And takshifu with tāʾ, active and passive both. The verb belongs to the Hour, or to the state, that is, the state or the Hour becomes severe." And it was read «يُكْشِفُ» with ḍamma on the yāʾ or tāʾ and kasra on the shīn, from akshafa, when one enters into uncovering. And "the man akshafa" means that his upper lip turned over, because what is beneath it is uncovered. The uncovering of the shin is a metonymy for severity; no one who has tasted the flavour of speech and heard the Arabs' sayings in their verse and prose doubts that. The rajaz poet said:
4309 - عَجِبْتُ مِنْ نفسي ومن إشفاقِها ... ومِنْ طِرادي الطيرَ عن أَرْزاقِها
في سَنَةٍ قد كَشَفَتْ عن ساقِها ... حمراءَ تَبْرِي اللحمَ عَنْ عُراقها
(I marvelled at myself and its fearfulness, and at my driving the birds away from their provisions, in a year that has uncovered its shin, a red one that strips the flesh from the bone.)
And Ḥātim al-Ṭāʾī said:
4310 - أخو الحربِ إنْ عَضَّتْ به الحربُ عَضَّها ... وإن شَمَّرَتْ عن ساقِها الحربُ شَمَّرا
(He is the brother of war: if war bites him he bites it, and if war tucks up its shin, he tucks up too.)
And another said:
4311 - كَشَفَتْ لهم عن ساقِها ... وبدا من الشَّرِّ الصُّراحُ
(She uncovered her shin for them, and the pure evil appeared.)
And another said:
4312 - قد شَمَّرَتْ عن ساقِها فَشُدُّوا ... وجَدَّت الحربُ بكم فَجُدُّوا
(War has tucked up its shin, so gird yourselves; war has become earnest with you, so be earnest.)
And another said:
4313 - صبراً أُمامُ إنَّه شرٌّ باقِ ... وقامَتِ الحربُ بنا على ساقِ
(Patience, Umāma! It is an enduring evil, and war has stood with us upon a shin.)
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The uncovering of the shin and the showing of the female attendants is a proverbial expression for the severity of a matter and the difficulty of a calamity. Its origin is in terror and rout, and in the veiled women tucking up their garments from their shins in war and showing their attendants at that time.
Ibn Qays al-Ruqayyāt said:
4314 - تُذْهِلُ الشيخَ عن بنيه وتُبْدي ... عن خِدام العَقِليةُ العَذْراءُ
(It makes the old man forget his sons, and the virgin, the noble lady, shows her anklets.)"
End of quotation. How excellent is what Abū al-Qāsim has shown of the connection underlying this figurative usage! Allah bless his skill. As for what the exegetes have cited, it is to be interpreted figuratively, and likewise the ḥadīth of Ibn Masʿūd and the like. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Whoever feels the harms of lacking this science knows the greatness of its benefits." End of quotation. He means the science of bayān (rhetoric).

semin-durr:43-43.t:
His saying: {خَاشِعَةً}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the nominative element of «يُدْعَوْن», and «أبصارُهم» is the agent of it. He attributed humility to the eyes, although all the limbs are the same, because its effect is apparent in them.
And His saying: {وَهُمْ سَالِمُونَ} is a ḥāl from the nominative element of the second «يُدْعَوْن».

semin-durr:44-44.t: His saying: {وَمَن يُكَذِّبُ}: it is accusative, either as a conjunction on the yāʾ (the attached pronoun), or as mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment), which is the weaker view because conjunction is possible without weakness. The i'rab of what follows it has already been given.

semin-durr:48-48.t:
His saying: {إِذْ نادى}: «إذ» is accusative by an omitted muḍāf, that is, "do not let your state be like his state, or your story like his story, at the time of his calling". What indicates the omitted element is that prohibition does not fall upon essences; it falls only upon their states and attributes.
His saying: {وَهُوَ مَكْظُومٌ} is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause from the pronoun in «نادى». Al-makẓūm means the one filled with grief and rage. Dhū al-Rumma said:
4315 - وأنتَ مِنْ حُبِّ مَيٍّ مُضْمِرٌ حُزْناً ... عاني الفؤادِ قريحُ القلبِ مكظومُ
(And you, out of love for Mayy, conceal grief, with a captive heart, a wounded heart, choking down your sorrow.)
Its root was discussed earlier in Āl ʿImrān.

semin-durr:49-49.t: His saying: {تَدَارَكَهُ}: Ubayy, ʿAbd Allāh and Ibn ʿAbbās read «تدارَكَتْه» with the feminine tāʾ, because of the wording (of «نعمة»). Al-Ḥasan, Ibn Hurmuz and al-Aʿmash read «تَدَّارَكُه» with shadda on the dāl; it was explained that the original is «تَتَدارَكُه» with two tāʾs, imperfect, and it was assimilated. This is irregular (shādhdh), because the first silent letter is not a letter of softness (līn); it is like al-Bazzī's reading {إِذْ تَلَقَّوْنَهُ} [al-Nūr: 15] and {نَاراً تلظى} [al-Layl: 14]. And this is on the portrayal of the state, because the story is in the past, so the use of the imperfect here is for portrayal.

semin-durr:51-51.t: His saying: {لَيُزْلِقُونَكَ}: Nāfiʿ read it with fatḥa on the yāʾ, and the rest with ḍamma. As for the reading of the majority, it is from azlaqahu, that is, "he made his foot slip"; the transitivity is by the hamza, from zalaqa yazliqu. As for Nāfiʿ's reading, the transitivity is by the vowel: one says zaliqa, with kasra, and zalaqtuhu, with fatḥa. A parallel is: shatirat ʿaynuhu, with kasra, and shataraha Allāh, with fatḥa; and several such sisters have already been mentioned. It was also said that zalaqahu and azlaqahu have a single meaning. The meaning of the verse concerns affliction by the evil eye, and in the exegesis there is a story. The bāʾ is either for transitivity, like the one entering on an instrument, that is, they made their eyes like the instrument that makes you slip, as in "I worked with the adze"; or it is for causation, that is, "because of their eyes". / His saying: {لَمَّا سَمِعُواْ الذكر}: whoever makes «لمّا» temporal makes it accusative by «يُزْلِقُونك», and whoever makes it a particle makes its apodosis omitted, as indicated, that is, "when they heard the Reminder they almost made you slip"; and whoever allows the apodosis to be placed first says that it is placed first here.

ukberi-tibyan:1-1.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ن وَالْقَلَمِ وَمَا يَسْطُرُونَ (١))
His saying (ن وَالْقَلَمِ): it is like «يس وَالْقُرْآنِ», and that has been mentioned.

ukberi-tibyan:14-15.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَنْ كَانَ ذَا مَالٍ وَبَنِينَ (١٤) إِذَا تُتْلَى عَلَيْهِ آيَاتُنَا قَالَ أَسَاطِيرُ الْأَوَّلِينَ (١٥))
His saying (أَنْ كَانَ) is read with kasra on the hamza [إِنْ], as a condition, and with fatḥa on it, as maṣdariyya. [On the first,] the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by (إِذَا تُتْلَى), i.e. "if he has wealth, he disbelieves". If you make it a maṣdar, the implied form is "because he has wealth, he disbelieves". Neither «تُتْلَى» nor «مَالٍ» can govern it, because what comes after إِذَا does not govern what precedes it.
«[Translator's note: the source text here reads «وَلَا) : «مَالٍ»», evidently garbled; the sense "nor مَالٍ" is followed. Perhaps «قَالَ» was intended.]»

ukberi-tibyan:17-17.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّا بَلَوْنَاهُمْ كَمَا بَلَوْنَا أَصْحَابَ الْجَنَّةِ إِذْ أَقْسَمُوا لَيَصْرِمُنَّهَا مُصْبِحِينَ (١٧))
And (مُصْبِحِينَ) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent in يَصْرِمُنَّهَا, not in أَقْسَمُوا.

ukberi-tibyan:25-25.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَغَدَوْا عَلَى حَرْدٍ قَادِرِينَ (٢٥))
And (عَلَى حَرْدٍ) is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «قَادِرِينَ», and «قَادِرِينَ» is a ḥāl (circumstantial).
It is also said: it is the khabar (predicate) of غَدَوْا, because it has been treated like أَصْبَحُوا.

ukberi-tibyan:34-34.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ جَنَّاتِ النَّعِيمِ (٣٤))
His saying (عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ): it may be an adverb (ẓarf) for the notion of settledness (al-istiqrār), and it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «جَنَّاتٍ».

ukberi-tibyan:39-39.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَمْ لَكُمْ أَيْمَانٌ عَلَيْنَا بَالِغَةٌ إِلَى يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ. . . (٣٩))
His saying (بَالِغَةٌ): in the nominative it is a naʿt (adjective) of أَيْمَانٌ; and in the accusative [بَالِغَةً] it is a ḥāl (circumstantial), what governs it being the first adverbial expression [لَكُمْ] or the second [عَلَيْنَا].

ukberi-tibyan:42-43.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَوْمَ يُكْشَفُ عَنْ سَاقٍ وَيُدْعَوْنَ إِلَى السُّجُودِ فَلَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ (٤٢) خَاشِعَةً أَبْصَارُهُمْ تَرْهَقُهُمْ ذِلَّةٌ وَقَدْ كَانُوا يُدْعَوْنَ إِلَى السُّجُودِ وَهُمْ سَالِمُونَ (٤٣))
His saying (يَوْمَ يُكْشَفُ), i.e. "remember the day when it is laid bare". It is also said: what governs it is «خَاشِعَةً».
It is also read «تَكْشِفُ», i.e. "[when] the terror of the Resurrection lays bare". And خَاشِعَةً is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «يُدْعَوْنَ».

ukberi-tibyan:44-44.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَذَرْنِي وَمَنْ يُكَذِّبُ بِهَذَا الْحَدِيثِ. . . (٤٤))
And (مَنْ يُكَذِّبُ) is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the object, or it is a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment).

ukberi-tibyan:6-6.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (بِأَيِّيكُمُ الْمَفْتُونُ (٦))
His saying (بِأَيِّيكُمُ الْمَفْتُونُ): there are three views on it. The first: the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida). The second: الْمَفْتُون is a maṣdar (verbal noun), like الْمَفْعُول and الْمَيْسُور, i.e. "in which of you is الْفُتُون", i.e. madness.
The third: it [the bāʾ] is in the sense of فِي, i.e. "in which group of you is madness".

ukberi-tibyan:9-9.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَدُّوا لَوْ تُدْهِنُ فَيُدْهِنُونَ (٩))
His saying (لَوْ تُدْهِنُ فَيُدْهِنُونَ): the nūn was kept only because He conjoined it to تُدْهِنُ and did not make it the answer to the wish; in some codices it is without the nūn [فَيُدْهِنُوا], as the answer.

zajjaj:14-14.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿أنْ كانَ ذا مالٍ وبَنِينَ﴾ ("because he is possessed of wealth and sons"). It has also been read in the form of a question, and the meaning is that of rebuke (tawbīkh). The position of «أنْ» is accusative (naṣb), on two lines: on the meaning "Is it because he is possessed of wealth and sons that he says, when Our verses are recited to him…?", so «أنْ» is accusative, meaning "he said that because he was possessed of wealth and sons"; that is, he made unbelief in Our signs the repayment for the blessing of wealth and sons he had been granted. When the alif of interrogation comes, this is the view, and nothing else is valid. And it was said in the exegesis: "And do not obey every despicable swearer of oaths … because he is possessed of wealth and sons", that is: do not obey him on account of his affluence and his numbers. And «أساطِيرُ» ("tales") is nominative (marfūʿ) by the implied «هِيَ» ("they are"); the meaning is: "When Our verses are recited to him, he says: they are the tales of the ancients." The singular of «الأساطِير» is «أُسْطُورَة».

zajjaj:16-16.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿سَنَسِمُهُ عَلى الخُرْطُومِ﴾ ("We shall brand him on the snout"): its meaning is "We shall brand him on his nose"; «الخُرْطُوم» is the nose. The meaning of «سَنَسِمُهُ» is: We shall give him in the Hereafter the mark by which the people of the Fire are known, namely the blackening of their faces. And it is possible — and Allah knows best — that He singles him out with a brand of his own, because of the extremity of his enmity to the Prophet (peace be upon him), so that he is marked out with a disfigurement by which he is distinguished from others, just as his enmity to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was an enmity by which he was distinguished from others.

zajjaj:17-17.t: His saying: ﴿إنّا بَلَوْناهم كَما بَلَوْنا أصْحابَ الجَنَّةِ إذْ أقْسَمُوا لَيَصْرِمُنَّها مُصْبِحِينَ﴾ ("We have tried them as We tried the owners of the garden, when they swore they would surely cut its fruit in the morning"). «الجَنَّة» is the orchard. These were a people in the region of Yemen. They had a father who used to give charity to the poor from his garden. It has come in the exegesis that he used to take from it his provision for the year and give the rest in charity; and it has also come that he used to leave for the poor whatever the sickle missed, whatever was at the bottom of the stacks, whatever the grape-pickers missed, and whatever fell outside the mat spread beneath the palm tree when its fruit was cut, so that a great deal would collect from that. His sons said: "We are many, and if we do with the poor what our father used to do, things will become hard for us." So they swore they would cut its fruit in the darkness before dawn (sudfa). Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿وَلا يَسْتَثْنُونَ﴾ [al-Qalam: 18] ("and they made no exception"), i.e. they swore and did not say "If Allah wills." When the time they had appointed came, in the darkness before dawn, they went early to their garden to cut its fruit.

zajjaj:19-19.t: His saying, the Exalted: ﴿فَطافَ عَلَيْها طائِفٌ مِن رَبِّكَ وهم نائِمُونَ﴾ ("Then there came upon it a visitation from your Lord while they slept"), i.e. He sent upon it a punishment from the sky, and it was burnt entirely.

zajjaj:20-20.t:
﴿فَأصْبَحَتْ كالصَّرِيمِ﴾ ("So it became like the cut-off [crop]"), i.e. it became black as the night.
﴿فَتَنادَوْا مُصْبِحِينَ﴾ [al-Qalam: 21] ﴿أنِ اغْدُوا عَلى حَرْثِكم إنْ كُنْتُمْ صارِمِينَ﴾ [al-Qalam: 22] ("And they called to one another in the morning: Go early to your crop if you would cut it"), i.e. if you are resolved upon cutting the dates.

zajjaj:23-23.t: ﴿فانْطَلَقُوا وهم يَتَخافَتُونَ﴾ ("So they set out, whispering to one another"), i.e. speaking secretly among themselves with ﴿أنْ لا يَدْخُلَنَّها اليَوْمَ عَلَيْكم مِسْكِينٌ﴾ [al-Qalam: 24] ("Let no poor person enter it upon you today"). «التَّخافُت» is speaking secretly.

zajjaj:25-25.t:
﴿وَغَدَوْا عَلى حَرْدٍ قادِرِينَ﴾ ("And they went early, ḥard, [thinking themselves] able"): from their saying «حارَدَتِ السَّنَةُ» ("the year was barren"), when it withholds its bounty. It was also said: "in anger". As for «الحَرْد» meaning purpose/heading towards, they recited concerning it:
؎أقْبَلَ سَيْلٌ جاءَ مِن أمْرِ اللَّهْ ∗∗∗ يَحْرِدُ حَرْدَ الجَنَّةِ المُغِلَّةْ
(A torrent came on, sent by Allah's command, making for the fruitful garden.)
That is: heading straight for the fruitful garden. ﴿فَلَمّا رَأوْها قالُوا إنّا لَضالُّونَ﴾ [al-Qalam: 26] ("But when they saw it, they said: Surely we have lost our way").

zajjaj:26-26.t: ﴿فَلَمّا رَأوْها﴾ ("But when they saw it") burnt, ﴿قالُوا إنّا لَضالُّونَ﴾ ("they said: Surely we have lost our way"), i.e. we have strayed from the path to our garden; that is: this is not it. Then they knew that it was a punishment, and they said: ﴿بَلْ نَحْنُ مَحْرُومُونَ﴾ [al-Qalam: 27] ("Nay, rather we have been deprived"), i.e. we have been deprived of the fruit of our garden because we withheld it from the poor.

zajjaj:28-28.t:
﴿قالَ أوْسَطُهم ألَمْ أقُلْ لَكم لَوْلا تُسَبِّحُونَ﴾ ("The most moderate of them said: Did I not say to you, why do you not glorify [Allah]?"). «أوْسَطُهُمْ» means the most just of them, from His saying: ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ جَعَلْناكم أُمَّةً وسَطًا﴾ [al-Baqara: 143] ("And thus We have made you a middle nation"), i.e. just. ﴿لَوْلا تُسَبِّحُونَ﴾: he said to them: make an exception (istithnāʾ) in your oath — because they had sworn they would cut its fruit in the morning and made no exception. The meaning of tasbīḥ (glorification) here is the exception, that is, saying "If Allah wills." If someone says: "tasbīḥ is saying 'Glory be to Allah (subḥān Allāh)'", the answer to that is that everything by which you magnify Allah is tasbīḥ, because tasbīḥ in the language — according to what has come from the Prophet (peace be upon him) — is declaring Allah free of every evil; and the exception is a magnification of Allah and an acknowledgement that no one is able to do any deed except by His will, Mighty and Majestic.
So the meaning of His saying ﴿إنّا بَلَوْناهم كَما بَلَوْنا أصْحابَ الجَنَّةِ﴾ [al-Qalam: 17] ("We have tried them as We tried the owners of the garden") is: We tried the people of Mecca when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ invoked against them, saying: «"O Allah, make Your tread heavy upon Muḍar, and make it upon them years like the years of Joseph"», and Allah tried them with scab, destruction and the loss of provisions, just as He tried the owners of this garden with its burning and the loss of their provision from it.

zajjaj:35-36.t: His saying: ﴿أفَنَجْعَلُ المُسْلِمِينَ كالمُجْرِمِينَ﴾ ﴿ما لَكم كَيْفَ تَحْكُمُونَ﴾ ("Shall We then treat those who submit like the criminals? What is wrong with you? How do you judge?"). This alif is the alif of interrogation, and its sense here is rebuke and making them acknowledge (taqrīr). It has come in the exegesis that one of the unbelievers of Quraysh said: "If what they mention is true, that they have a share in the Hereafter, then we shall have in the Hereafter more than that, just as in this world we are better off than they are." So Allah rebuked them, saying: ﴿أفَنَجْعَلُ المُسْلِمِينَ كالمُجْرِمِينَ﴾, and likewise ﴿ما لَكم كَيْفَ تَحْكُمُونَ﴾, meaning: "On which of the states of unbelief do you base your judgement?!"

zajjaj:37-38.t: ﴿أمْ لَكم كِتابٌ فِيهِ تَدْرُسُونَ﴾ ﴿إنَّ لَكم فِيهِ لَما تَخَيَّرُونَ﴾ ("Or do you have a scripture in which you study, that you shall surely have in it whatever you choose?"), i.e. do you have a scripture from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, stating that you shall have whatever you choose?!

zajjaj:39-39.t: ﴿أمْ لَكم أيْمانٌ عَلَيْنا بالِغَةٌ﴾ ("Or do you have oaths binding on Us, bāligha"): it means "confirmed"; ﴿إلى يَوْمِ القِيامَةِ إنَّ لَكم لَما تَحْكُمُونَ﴾ ("until the Day of Resurrection, that you shall have whatever you judge?"), i.e. a sworn oath upon what you claim in your judgement.

zajjaj:40-40.t: His saying: ﴿سَلْهم أيُّهم بِذَلِكَ زَعِيمٌ﴾ ("Ask them which of them is the guarantor of that"). «الزَّعِيم» is the surety and the guarantor; the meaning is: "Ask them which of them has stood surety for that?!"

zajjaj:41-42.t:
His saying: ﴿أمْ لَهم شُرَكاءُ فَلْيَأْتُوا بِشُرَكائِهِمْ إنْ كانُوا صادِقِينَ﴾ ﴿يَوْمَ يُكْشَفُ عَنْ ساقٍ﴾ ("Or do they have partners? Then let them bring their partners, if they are truthful — on the Day when the shin is laid bare"), i.e. let them bring their partners on the Day of Resurrection. The meaning of ﴿يُكْشَفُ عَنْ ساقٍ﴾ in the language is: the grave matter is laid bare. The poet said:
؎قَدْ شَمَّرَتْ عَنْ ساقِها فَشُدُّوا ∗∗∗ وجَدَّتِ الحَرْبُ بِكم فَجِدُّوا
؎والقَوْسُ فِيها وتَرٌ عُرُدُ
(War has bared its shin, so brace yourselves; war has grown earnest with you, so be earnest — and the bow has a tough, taut string.)
And it has come in the exegesis from Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, who said: my father narrated to us, he said: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar — meaning Ghundar — narrated to us, from Shuʿba, from Mughīra, from Ibrāhīm, who said: Ibn ʿAbbās said concerning His saying ﴿يُكْشَفُ عَنْ ساقٍ﴾: "[It is laid bare] from the grave matter." And Ibn Masʿūd said: "The All-Merciful will uncover His shin; as for the believers, they will fall down before Him prostrating, and as for the hypocrites, their backs will become one rigid piece (ṭabaqan ṭabaqan), as though there were skewers in them." This is what we have narrated in the exegesis, and what the lexicographers have said.
[Translator's note: the isnad as printed begins «عَنْ أحْمَدَ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ أحْمَدَ بْنِ حَنْبَلَ … ثَنا أبِي»; the narrator from Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal is normally his son ʿAbd Allāh, so the chain may be garbled in the source. Translated as written.]
Abū Isḥāq said: This is the interpretation of His saying: ﴿وَيُدْعَوْنَ إلى السُّجُودِ فَلا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ﴾ ﴿خاشِعَةً أبْصارُهُمْ﴾ [al-Qalam: 43] ("and they will be called to prostrate, but they will not be able — their eyes downcast"); the hypocrites are meant by it.
And His saying: ﴿تَرْهَقُهم ذِلَّةٌ﴾ [al-Qalam: 43] means: abasement will cover them; ﴿وَقَدْ كانُوا يُدْعَوْنَ إلى السُّجُودِ وهم سالِمُونَ﴾ [al-Qalam: 43] ("and they used to be called to prostrate while they were sound"): what is meant by it is: in this world.

zajjaj:44-44.t: His saying: ﴿فَذَرْنِي ومَن يُكَذِّبُ بِهَذا الحَدِيثِ﴾ ("So leave Me with whoever denies this discourse"); and similar to it is ﴿ذَرْنِي ومَن خَلَقْتُ وحِيدًا﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 11] ("Leave Me with the one I created alone"). Its meaning is: do not occupy your heart with him; leave him to Me, for I shall requite him. Similar to it is a man's saying: "Leave me and him" — it does not mean that he was preventing him from doing so; rather its interpretation is: "Leave him to me, for I shall spare you the trouble of him."

zajjaj:48-48.t:
His saying: ﴿فاصْبِرْ لِحُكْمِ رَبِّكَ ولا تَكُنْ كَصاحِبِ الحُوتِ﴾ ("So be patient for the judgement of your Lord, and do not be like the companion of the fish"): He means Jonah (peace be upon him).
﴿إذْ نادى وهو مَكْظُومٌ﴾ ("when he called out while he was makẓūm"), i.e. filled with grief and distress.

zajjaj:49-49.t:
His saying: ﴿لَوْلا أنْ تَدارَكَهُ نِعْمَةٌ مِن رَبِّهِ لَنُبِذَ بِالعَراءِ وهو مَذْمُومٌ﴾ ("Had not a favour from his Lord reached him, he would have been cast onto the barren shore while blameworthy"). The meaning is that he was cast onto the barren shore while not blameworthy; what shows this is that the favour had encompassed him.
And His saying: ﴿فاجْتَباهُ رَبُّهُ﴾ [al-Qalam: 50] ("But his Lord chose him"): this is a clearing of him from blame. «العَراء» is the empty place. The poet said:
؎رَفَعْتُ رِجْلًا لا أخافُ عِثارَها ∗∗∗ ونَبَذْتُ بِالبَلَدِ العَراءِ ثِيابِي
(I lifted a foot whose stumbling I did not fear, and cast off my clothes in the barren land.)

zajjaj:51-51.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَإنْ يَكادُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَيُزْلِقُونَكَ بِأبْصارِهِمْ﴾ ("And those who disbelieve would almost make you slip with their eyes"). It was also read «لَيُزْهِقُونَكَ» with hāʾ, but this — I mean the hāʾ — contradicts the Muṣḥaf, and the reading follows what agrees with the Muṣḥaf. This verse needs a section of explanation from the language. As for what has been narrated in the exegesis: it is narrated that when a man of the Arabs wanted to strike something with the evil eye (yaʿtān), i.e. afflict it with the eye, he would starve himself for three days, then say to what he wanted to strike with the eye: "I have not seen camels — or sheep, or whatever he wanted — like today's!" The meaning is: "I have not seen camels like the camels I see today." By this saying he would afflict them with the eye. So they said to the Prophet ﷺ, when they heard the Reminder from him, what they used to say to whatever they wanted to strike with the eye.
As for the doctrine of the lexicographers, the interpretation according to them is that out of the intensity of their hatred and hostility towards you, they almost harm you with their looking — the look of hatred. This is used in speech; one says: "He looked at me with a look that almost floored me," and "a look with which he almost devoured me." Its interpretation in every case is that he looked at me with a look such that, had he been able along with it to devour me or floor me, he would have done so. This is clear and evident, and Allah knows best.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat Nūn
Makkan
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿ن والقَلَمِ وما يَسْطُرُونَ﴾ — it was read with the nūn assimilated into the wāw; it was read with the nūn pronounced distinctly before the wāw; and it was read ”نُونَ والقَلَمِ“ with a fatḥa on the nūn. The one who chose assimilating the nūn into the wāw (did so), whether the wāw [Translator's note: so printed; the nūn is evidently meant] is quiescent or vowelled, because what has come in the exegesis removes it from being quiescent and pronounced distinctly; for whoever makes it quiescent and pronounces it distinctly only treats it as a letter of the alphabet, whereas the one who assimilates it may assimilate it while it carries a fatḥa. [Translator's note: the passage is compressed in the text as transmitted.] It has come in the exegesis that ”نُونْ“ is the whale on which the seven earths were spread out; and it has also come in the exegesis that the nūn is the inkwell. It has not come in the exegesis in the way I interpreted the letters of the alphabet; and quiescence is only permissible if it is a letter of the alphabet. It has come in the exegesis that the first thing Allah created was the Pen, and He said to it: (Write). It said: "O Lord, and what shall I write?" He said: (The decree). So the Pen ran with all that will be until the Day of Resurrection; and among what the Pen ran with was: ﴿تَبَّتْ يَدا أبِي لَهَبٍ﴾ [al-Masad: 1]. His saying: ﴿وَما يَسْطُرُونَ﴾ means: and what the angels write.

zajjaj:2-2.t: His saying: ﴿ما أنْتَ بِنِعْمَةِ رَبِّكَ بِمَجْنُونٍ﴾ — this is a question from the chapters of grammar which needs explanation. His saying ”أنْتَ“ is the ism (subject) of ”ما“, and ”بِمَجْنُونٍ“ is the khabar (predicate), and ”بِنِعْمَةِ رَبِّكَ“ is connected with the sense of negation. The meaning is: "Madness is negated from you by the favour of your Lord," just as you say "أنْتَ بِنِعْمَةِ اللَّهِ فَهِمٌ" (by the favour of Allah you are intelligent) and "ما أنْتَ بِنِعْمَةِ اللَّهِ جاهِلٌ" (by the favour of Allah you are not ignorant), its interpretation being: "ignorance has left you by the favour of your Lord." This is a reply to their saying: ﴿وَقالُوا يا أيُّها الَّذِي نُـزِّلَ عَلَيْهِ الذِّكْرُ إنَّكَ لَمَجْنُونٌ﴾ [al-Ḥijr: 6].

zajjaj:3-3.t: His saying: ﴿وَإنَّ لَكَ لأجْرًا غَيْرَ مَمْنُونٍ﴾ means: not cut off; and it has come in the exegesis: "not counted."

zajjaj:4-4.t: ﴿وَإنَّكَ لَعَلى خُلُقٍ عَظِيمٍ﴾ — it is said: upon Islam; and it is said: upon the Quran. The meaning — and Allah knows best — is: "You are upon the character which Allah commanded you in the Quran."

zajjaj:5-5.t:
His saying: ﴿فَسَتُبْصِرُ ويُبْصِرُونَ﴾ ﴿بِأيِّيكُمُ المَفْتُونُ﴾ [al-Qalam: 6] — the meaning of ”اَلْمَفْتُونُ“ is: the one who has been afflicted with madness. Abū ʿUbayda said: the bāʾ is meant to be discarded; the meaning is "which of you is the afflicted one." He said: and like it is the saying of the poet:
؎نَضْرِبُ بِالسَّيْفِ ونَرْجُو بِالفَرَجِ
(We strike with the sword and hope for relief.)
He said its meaning is "we hope for relief." But it is not so; the meaning is "we hope for the removal of what we are in by relief," or "we hope for victory by relief." The bāʾ in ”بِأيِّكُمُ المَفْتُونُ“ cannot be redundant (laghw); that is not permissible in Arabic in the view of any of its authorities. There are two views on it among the grammarians. They said ”اَلْمَفْتُونُ“ here is in the sense of ”اَلْفُتُونُ“ (affliction): maṣdars (verbal nouns) come on the pattern of the passive participle. The Arabs say "لَيْسَ لِهَذا مَعْقُولٌ", i.e. intelligence (ʿaql), and "لَيْسَ لَهُ مَعْقُودُ رَأْيٍ" in the sense of "firmness of opinion (ʿaqd raʾy)," and you say "دَعْهُ إلى مَيْسُورٍ" in the sense of "to ease (yusr)." So the meaning is: "You will see and they will see in which of you is the affliction." There is another view: "in which of you is the afflicted one" — in the party you are in, or in the party of the disbelievers among whom are Abū Jahl, al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra al-Makhzūmī and those like them. On this view the meaning is: "You will see and they will see in which of the two parties the madman is: in the party of Islam or in the party of disbelief."

zajjaj:9-9.t: His saying: ﴿وَدُّوا لَوْ تُدْهِنُ فَيُدْهِنُونَ﴾ means: "They wish that you would compromise with them in religion, so that they would compromise with you."

zajjaj:10-10.t: His saying: ﴿وَلا تُطِعْ كُلَّ حَلافٍ مَهِينٍ﴾ — (”مَهِينٍ“ is on the pattern) ”فَعِيلٌ“ from ”اَلْمَهانَةُ“, which is paltriness; its meaning here is paltriness of judgement and discernment.

zajjaj:11-11.t: His saying: ﴿هَمّازٍ مَشّاءٍ بِنَمِيمٍ﴾ — ”اَلْهَمّازُ“ is the one who backbites people.

zajjaj:12-12.t:
His saying: ﴿مَنّاعٍ لِلْخَيْرِ مُعْتَدٍ أثِيمٍ﴾ — its meaning is: he used to hold back his family, his children and his kin from Islam. It has come in the exegesis that he was al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra al-Makhzūmī; he was well-off and of great wealth, and he had ten sons, and he used to say to them and to his kin: "Whoever of you embraces Islam, I will withhold my support from him."

His saying: ﴿مُعْتَدٍ أثِيمٍ﴾ means: exceeding the bounds in wrongdoing. ”أثِيمٍ“ means: sinful towards his Lord, i.e. sinful through his transgression and his offence.

zajjaj:13-13.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿عُتُلٍّ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ زَنِيمٍ﴾ — it has come in the exegesis that the ʿutull here is the one fierce in disputing; and it has come in the exegesis that he is the coarse of character, base of nature. In the language it is the rough and coarse one. As for ”اَلزَّنِيمُ“, it has come in the language that he is the one attached to a people while not being one of them. Ḥassān ibn Thābit al-Anṣārī said:
؎وَأنْتَ زَنِيمٌ نِيطَ في آلِ هاشِمٍ ∗∗∗ كَما نِيطَ خَلْفَ الرّاكِبِ القَدَحُ الفَرْدُ
(You are an adventitious hanger-on, attached to the family of Hāshim, as the lone cup is tied on behind the rider.)
And it is said that the zanīm is the one known for evil, as a goat is known by its wattle (zanama); ”اَلزَّنَمَتانِ“ are the two wattles hanging at the throats of goats.
